<!-- source: README.md -->
# callai

callai runs one prompt through any coding-agent CLI and gives you the answer in one consistent shape.

Claude Code, Codex, opencode, pi, Hermes and Grok each have their own flags, output formats, permission
models and quirks. callai turns one command into the right invocation for each, runs it without
interaction, and returns the same text, JSON or event stream whichever harness answered. Use it from a
shell, a script, CI, another AI agent, or Python.

```bash
callai -n codex -p "Reply with exactly: pong"
```

```text
pong
```

```bash
callai -n claude-code/codex/grok -p "Explain main.py" -o json     # three harnesses at once
```

## Features

- **One interface, six harnesses:** `claude-code`, `codex`, `opencode`, `pi`, `hermes`, `grok`, chosen
  with `-n`. Everything else (prompt, model, permissions, sessions) is spelled the same for all of them.
- **Machine-readable output:** `-o json` gives one normalised result (`text`, `is_error`,
  `session_id`, `usage`, …). `-o stream-json` streams `start`, `text`, `tool_use`, `tool_result` and
  `result` events as they happen.
- **Permission levels:** `--permission read-only|auto|bypass`, mapped to each harness's own flags and
  checked by running real tool calls. callai refuses a level a harness can't honour rather than run
  with more access.
- **Sessions:** `--resume SESSION_ID` and `--continue` pick a conversation back up.
- **Fan-out:** `-n a/b/c` runs several harnesses at the same time, `-n a,b,c` one after another, and
  `-n all` every installed one.
- **Scriptable:** predictable exit codes, `--dry-run` to see the exact command, and it never hangs on
  an idle stdin.
- **Python API:** `callai.run("codex", "…")` returns the same result. No runtime dependencies.

them in one file. Project design notes are in [`docs/DESIGN.md`](../DESIGN.md), and release history is in
[`CHANGELOG.md`](../../CHANGELOG.md).

<!-- source: getting-started/why-callai.md -->
# Why callai

callai gives every coding-agent CLI the same non-interactive interface, so you can switch harnesses
or use several without rewriting the code that calls them.

## The problem

Each coding agent can run a single prompt without a chat window. They all do it differently:

| You want | claude | codex | opencode | grok |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Run one prompt | `claude -p -- P` | `codex exec -- P` | `opencode run -- P` | `grok --single=P` |
| JSON output | `--output-format json` (one object) | `--json` (event lines) | `--format json` (event lines) | `--output-format json` (one object) |
| Read-only | `--permission-mode plan` | `--sandbox read-only` | none | `--tools read_file,grep,list_dir …` |
| Continue a session | `--resume ID` | `exec … resume ID` | `--session ID` | `--resume=ID` |
| Where the answer is | `.result` | last `agent_message` item | `text` parts | `.text` |

Each harness also has its own edge cases:
- a prompt starting with `-` can be taken as a flag;
- grok runs a prompt starting with `/` as a slash command;
- opencode wraps any argument containing a space in quotes before sending it;
- hermes prints tool previews mixed into the answer;
- some harnesses read your stdin, so a script's open pipe can stall them.

Code that drives one harness doesn't carry over to the next.

## What callai does

You write the call once:

```bash
callai -n codex -p "Fix the failing test" --permission auto -o json
```

callai builds the exact command line for the harness you chose, runs it with no prompts and no
interactive input, and turns whatever it prints into the same result:

```json
{"harness_name": "codex", "text": "…", "is_error": false, "exit_code": 0, "session_id": "…", "usage": {"input_tokens": 11, "output_tokens": 2}, "…": "…"}
```

Change `-n codex` to `-n grok` and nothing else changes, including the JSON your code reads.

## When to use it

- **Scripts and CI** that call a coding agent and need a reliable answer and exit code.
- **AI agents and orchestrators** that hand subtasks to other agents and parse the result.
- **Comparing harnesses or models** on the same prompt (`-n all`).
- **Not being locked in**: switch harness with one flag.

## When you don't need it

- You only ever use one harness interactively: use that harness directly.
- You need a harness feature callai doesn't model: pass it through after `--`
  (`callai -n opencode -p "…" -- --agent build`), or call the harness itself.
- You want an SDK for building agents (tools, memory, planning). callai drives existing agent CLIs; it
  doesn't build new ones.

## Design principles

- **Thin.** callai adds no behaviour of its own between you and the harness: no retries, no prompt
  rewriting, no hidden flags. `--dry-run` prints exactly what will run.
- **Fail closed.** If a harness can't honour an option, callai refuses (exit 2) instead of running with
  more access or quietly ignoring it.
- **Verified.** Every adapter is checked against the real harness CLI, and every permission level by
  scripted tool calls. A shared conformance suite pins the behaviour.
- **No dependencies.** Python standard library only.

Next: [Installation](installation.md) · See also: [Architecture](../concepts/architecture.md)

<!-- source: getting-started/installation.md -->
# Installation

Install callai itself, then the harness CLIs you want it to drive.

## Requirements

- Python 3.11 or newer. callai has no runtime dependencies.
- macOS or Linux. Windows works, except that `callai -p TEXT` can block on a stdin pipe that never
  closes. See the [FAQ](../faq.md#callai-hangs-on-windows-when-run-from-a-script).
- At least one harness CLI on your `PATH`, signed in or configured with an API key.

## Install callai

callai is not on PyPI yet (its distribution name will be `callai-cli`). Install it from a clone of the
repository, as a tool on your `PATH`:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/sugatoray/callai.git
uv tool install ./callai
callai --version
```

```text
callai 0.9.0
```

Or into a virtual environment with pip, which also makes the Python API importable:

```bash
python3 -m venv .venv
.venv/bin/pip install ./callai
.venv/bin/callai --version
```

## Install the harnesses

Install only the ones you'll use. Each harness needs its own sign-in or API key: callai uses whatever
the harness is already configured with.

| `-n` name | Binary | Install |
|---|---|---|
| `claude-code` | `claude` | `npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code` ([docs](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/setup)) |
| `codex` | `codex` | `npm install -g @openai/codex` ([docs](https://developers.openai.com/codex/cli)) |
| `opencode` | `opencode` | `npm install -g opencode-ai` ([docs](https://opencode.ai/docs/)) |
| `pi` | `pi` | `npm install -g @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent` ([docs](https://pi.dev/docs/latest/quickstart)) |
| `hermes` | `hermes` | `uv tool install hermes-agent` ([docs](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/)) |
| `grok` | `grok` | `npm install -g @xai-official/grok` ([docs](https://x.ai/cli)) |

From the project folder, the Makefile installs all of them at the versions callai was verified
against:

```bash
cd callai
make install.harnesses        # or one: make install.codex
```

> [!WARNING]
> `npm install -g @vibe-kit/grok-cli` also installs a `grok` command, but it is a different program
> with different flags, and callai doesn't support it. Use xAI's `@xai-official/grok`.

## Check what's installed

```bash
callai --list-harnesses
```

```text
claude-code  claude     2.1.316 (Claude Code)  /opt/node22/bin/claude
codex        codex      codex-cli 0.166.0  /opt/node22/bin/codex
opencode     opencode   1.19.5  /opt/node22/bin/opencode
pi           pi         1.4.0  /opt/node22/bin/pi
hermes       hermes     Hermes Agent v0.19.0 (2026.7.20)  /root/.local/bin/hermes
grok         grok       grok 1.0.70 (f50904eaee6c)  /opt/node22/bin/grok
```

A harness that isn't installed shows `not installed (see <install URL>)` instead.

Next: [Quickstart](quickstart.md) · Previous: [Why callai](why-callai.md)

<!-- source: getting-started/quickstart.md -->
# Quickstart

Run a prompt, get JSON back, and see exactly what callai runs, in five minutes.

**You'll need:** callai and at least one harness installed and signed in ([Installation](installation.md)).
The examples use `codex`; any `-n` name works.

## 1. Ask something

```bash
callai -n codex -p "Reply with exactly: pong"
```

```text
pong
```

Only the answer is printed. Tool previews, banners and progress output are removed. The exit code is
the harness's own: `0` here.

## 2. Get JSON

```bash
callai -n codex -p "Reply with exactly: pong" -o json
```

```json
{
  "harness_name": "codex",
  "model": null,
  "text": "pong",
  "exit_code": 0,
  "is_error": false,
  "duration_ms": 6979,
  "session_id": "01a19506-c5ee-7893-ab89-d0f6b04924a4",
  "usage": {"input_tokens": 11, "output_tokens": 2},
  "cost_usd": null,
  "argv": ["codex", "exec", "--json", "--skip-git-repo-check", "--", "Reply with exactly: pong"]
}
```

The same keys come back for every harness. A value the harness doesn't report is `null`: `model` is
`null` here because no `-m` was given and codex doesn't report the model it used. `argv` is the exact
command that ran.

## 3. See the command without running it

```bash
callai -n claude-code -m haiku -p "Explain main.py" --permission auto --dry-run
```

```text
claude -p --output-format json --model haiku --permission-mode acceptEdits -- 'Explain main.py'
```

`--dry-run` doesn't need the harness to be installed. Use it to check what a flag turns into.

## 4. Pipe something in

```bash
git diff | callai -n codex -p "Review this diff"
```

Piped text is appended to the prompt after a blank line. With no `-p` at all, the piped text *is* the
prompt.

## 5. Try another harness

```bash
callai -n claude-code -p "Reply with exactly: pong"
callai -n claude-code/codex -p "Reply with exactly: pong"      # both, at the same time
```

```text
pong
== claude-code ==
pong
== codex ==
pong
```

## Where next

- Learn everything step by step: [Tutorial](../tutorial/README.md).
- Calling callai from another agent? [Call callai from an AI agent](../guides/use-from-an-ai-agent.md).
- Look up a flag: [Command line reference](../reference/cli.md).

Previous: [Installation](installation.md)

# Tutorial

A step-by-step path through callai, from the first prompt to fan-out and the Python API.

Each step builds on the one before and takes a few minutes. Every command can be pasted into a
terminal as-is, and each one shows its real output. Read in order the first time; afterwards, the
[Reference](../reference/README.md) is quicker for looking things up.

**You'll need:** callai and at least one harness installed and signed in. See
[Installation](../getting-started/installation.md). Most steps use `codex` or `claude-code`, but any
harness works; where one behaves differently, the step says so.

1. [Run your first prompt](01-first-prompt.md): choose a harness, pass a prompt, read the answer.
2. [Get machine-readable output](02-json-output.md): `-o json`, exit codes and using the result in scripts.
3. [Control what the agent may do](03-permissions.md): `--permission` levels.
4. [Watch a run as it happens](04-streaming.md): `-o stream-json` events.
5. [Continue a conversation](05-sessions.md): `--resume` and `--continue`.
6. [Ask several harnesses at once](06-fan-out.md): `-n a/b/c`, `-n a,b,c`, `-n all`.
7. [Set your defaults](07-defaults.md): environment variables, the config file and model aliases.
8. [Use callai from Python](08-python-api.md): `callai.run()` and event callbacks.

Start: [1. Run your first prompt](01-first-prompt.md)

<!-- source: tutorial/01-first-prompt.md -->
# 1. Run your first prompt

Choose a harness with `-n`, pass a prompt with `-p`, and read the answer on stdout.

**You'll need:** callai and one harness installed ([Installation](../getting-started/installation.md)).

## Run it

```bash
callai -n claude-code -p "Reply with exactly: pong"
```

```text
pong
```

Here is what happened:

1. `-n claude-code` chose the harness. The names are `claude-code`, `codex`, `opencode`, `pi`, `hermes`
   and `grok`.
2. callai built the command `claude -p --output-format json -- 'Reply with exactly: pong'`. It asks
   every harness for its structured output, so the answer is never scraped from screen text.
3. It ran `claude` with no interactive input, in its own process group, and waited for it to finish.
4. It took the answer out of claude's JSON and printed only that, followed by a newline.

`-p` has three aliases (`-c`, `--prompt` and `--command`), so `claude -p` habits carry over.

## Choose a model

`-m` passes a model to the harness exactly as you type it:

```bash
callai -n claude-code -m haiku -p "Reply with exactly: pong"
callai -n opencode -m anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5 -p "Reply with exactly: pong"
```

Each harness has its own model names. opencode and pi want `provider/model`, and the others take a
name or id. Without `-m`, the harness uses its own default. To give one name a different meaning per
harness, see [model aliases](07-defaults.md#name-models-once-with-aliases).

## See the exact command

```bash
callai -n claude-code -m haiku -p "Reply with exactly: pong" --dry-run
```

```text
claude -p --output-format json --model haiku -- 'Reply with exactly: pong'
```

`--dry-run` prints the command and exits 0 without running anything. The harness doesn't even need
to be installed.

## Prompts that look like flags

callai always puts the prompt last, after `--` or as one `--option=PROMPT` argument, so a prompt such
as `-v is broken` reaches the model as text. Three harnesses would treat certain prompts as commands,
and callai refuses those (exit 2) rather than send them:

- grok runs a prompt starting with `/` as a slash command;
- pi reads a prompt starting with `@` as a file to attach;
- both have no escape, so start the prompt with other text.

## Pass extra flags to the harness

Anything after a bare `--` goes to the harness unchanged:

```bash
callai -n opencode -p "Explain main.py" --dry-run -- --agent build
```

```text
opencode run --format json --print-logs --log-level ERROR --agent build -- Explain main.py
```

Put callai's own flags before `--`. Everything after it belongs to the harness: had `--dry-run` come
after `--`, opencode would have received it, and callai would have run opencode instead of printing
the command.

## Recap

- `callai -n HARNESS -p PROMPT` runs one prompt and prints the answer.
- `-m` is passed through verbatim; each harness has its own model names.
- `--dry-run` shows the exact command; arguments after `--` go to the harness.

Reference: [`-n`](../reference/cli.md#-n-harness_name---name-harness_name) · [`-p`](../reference/cli.md#-p-prompt---prompt-prompt) · [`--dry-run`](../reference/cli.md#--dry-run)

Next: [2. Get machine-readable output](02-json-output.md) · Up: [Tutorial](README.md)

<!-- source: tutorial/02-json-output.md -->
# 2. Get machine-readable output

`-o json` returns one normalised result object, and the exit code tells you whether the run worked.

**You'll need:** [step 1](01-first-prompt.md).

## One JSON object

```bash
callai -n codex -p "Reply with exactly: pong" -o json
```

```json
{
  "harness_name": "codex",
  "model": null,
  "text": "pong",
  "exit_code": 0,
  "is_error": false,
  "duration_ms": 6979,
  "session_id": "01a19506-c5ee-7893-ab89-d0f6b04924a4",
  "usage": {"input_tokens": 11, "output_tokens": 2},
  "cost_usd": null,
  "argv": ["codex", "exec", "--json", "--skip-git-repo-check", "--", "Reply with exactly: pong"]
}
```

callai prints it on one line; it's spread out here for reading. The fields you'll use most:

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `text` | The final answer, or the error message when `is_error` is true. |
| `is_error` | Whether the run failed: from the harness's own error signal, or a non-zero exit. |
| `exit_code` | The harness's exit code. |
| `session_id` | Pass it to `--resume` to continue the conversation ([step 5](05-sessions.md)). |
| `usage` | Tokens, with `input_tokens` counting cache reads and writes too. `null` if unknown. |
| `model` | The model the harness says it used, else the one you asked for. |

Every field is described in the [output reference](../reference/output.md#-o-json).

## Use it in a script

```bash
answer=$(callai -n codex -p "Reply with exactly: pong" -o json < /dev/null | jq -r .text)
echo "$answer"
```

```text
pong
```

Redirect stdin (`< /dev/null`) in scripts. With `-p`, callai waits up to 3 seconds for piped input
when stdin is a pipe with nothing on it. This happens when a script or agent runs callai with an open,
silent stdin. It then warns and carries on, but the redirect skips the wait.

## Exit codes

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `0` | The harness succeeded. |
| harness's own | The harness failed with that code; `is_error` is `true`. |
| `1` | The harness reported an error but exited 0 (e.g. grok refusing a tool call). |
| `2` | Usage error: bad flag, no prompt, an option the harness can't honour. Nothing ran. |
| `124` | `--timeout` expired; the harness and everything it started were killed. |
| `127` | The harness isn't installed. |
| `130` | Interrupted with Ctrl-C. |

A failure still prints a result with `-o json`:

```bash
callai -n claude-code -m not-a-real-model-xyz -p hi -o json
echo "exit=$?"
```

```text
{"harness_name": "claude-code", "model": "not-a-real-model-xyz", "text": "There's an issue with the selected model (not-a-real-model-xyz). It may not exist or you may not have access to it. Run --model to pick a different model.", "exit_code": 1, "is_error": true, …}
exit=1
```

The harness's own stderr is shown on callai's stderr when a run fails. Add `-v` to see it live
on every run.

## Raw output

`-o raw` skips parsing and prints the harness's own stdout and stderr unchanged, byte for byte. It's
useful for debugging an adapter, and nothing else.

## Recap

- `-o json` gives the same object for every harness; `text` and `is_error` are the essentials.
- Check the exit code: `2` means nothing ran, `124` timeout, `127` not installed.
- Use `< /dev/null` when a script runs callai.

Reference: [Output formats](../reference/output.md) · [Exit codes and errors](../reference/errors.md)

Next: [3. Control what the agent may do](03-permissions.md) · Previous: [1. Run your first prompt](01-first-prompt.md)

<!-- source: tutorial/03-permissions.md -->
# 3. Control what the agent may do

`--permission` sets one level (`read-only`, `auto` or `bypass`) that callai translates into each
harness's own flags.

**You'll need:** [step 2](02-json-output.md).

## The four levels

| Level | Intent |
|---|---|
| `default` | Add nothing: the harness's own default applies. |
| `read-only` | Read and search files; no writes, no shell. |
| `auto` | Edit files in the working directory without asking. |
| `bypass` | Run every tool call without asking, shell included. |

## See what a level turns into

```bash
callai -n codex -p "Fix the failing test" --permission read-only --dry-run
callai -n codex -p "Fix the failing test" --permission auto --dry-run
callai -n pi -p "Fix the failing test" --permission auto --dry-run
```

```text
codex exec --json --skip-git-repo-check --sandbox read-only -- 'Fix the failing test'
codex exec --json --skip-git-repo-check --sandbox workspace-write -- 'Fix the failing test'
pi --mode json --tools read,grep,find,ls,edit,write --no-mcp -- 'Fix the failing test'
```

codex uses its sandbox. pi gets a tool allowlist: read and search tools, plus `edit` and `write`, but
no shell.

## When a harness can't honour a level

callai refuses instead of running with more access than you asked for:

```bash
callai -n opencode -p "Fix the failing test" --permission read-only
```

```text
callai: error: --permission read-only: opencode has no read-only mode (its plan agent still allows shell commands); pass `-- --agent plan` yourself if that is acceptable
```

The exit code is 2, and nothing ran. Some refusals mention a harness flag you can pass yourself after
`--` if its behaviour is acceptable to you.

## What each level really allows

callai's levels were checked by running scripted tool calls (file writes and shell commands, inside
and outside the working directory) against every harness:

| Level | claude-code | codex | opencode | pi | grok | hermes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `read-only` | plan mode: no writes, no shell | read-only sandbox | refused | read tools only | read tools only | refused |
| `auto` | edits inside the workspace | writes inside the workspace (sandboxed shell) | refused | file writes/edits, no shell | file writes/edits, no shell | file writes/edits, no shell |
| `bypass` | everything | everything | everything | everything | everything | everything |

> [!WARNING]
> With `default`, opencode, pi and hermes already write files and run shell commands without asking.
> claude-code, codex and grok don't. If an unattended run must not change anything, ask for
> `read-only` explicitly.

> [!CAUTION]
> grok's `auto` and `bypass` can write **outside** the working directory. To confine grok to the
> workspace, add its sandbox yourself (Linux needs bubblewrap):
> `callai -n grok -p "…" --permission auto -- --sandbox workspace`.
> See [Permissions](../concepts/permissions.md#grok-and-the-working-directory).

## `bypass` warns you

```bash
callai -n codex -p "Reply with exactly: pong" --permission bypass
```

```text
callai: warning: --permission bypass: codex will run every tool call without asking, including shell commands and writes outside the working directory.
pong
```

The warning goes to stderr, so it doesn't mix into the answer.

## Recap

- One flag, four levels, translated per harness; `--dry-run` shows the translation.
- A level a harness can't honour is refused with exit 2. callai never quietly grants more access.
- `default` means the harness's own default, which for some harnesses is permissive.

Reference: [`--permission`](../reference/cli.md#--permission-level) · Concept: [Permissions](../concepts/permissions.md)

Next: [4. Watch a run as it happens](04-streaming.md) · Previous: [2. Get machine-readable output](02-json-output.md)

<!-- source: tutorial/04-streaming.md -->
# 4. Watch a run as it happens

`-o stream-json` prints one JSON event per line while the harness works: what it says, which tools it
calls, and what they return, followed by the result.

**You'll need:** [step 2](02-json-output.md).

## Stream a run

```bash
callai -n pi -m stub/stub-model -p "Reply with exactly: pong" -o stream-json
```

```json
{"type": "start", "harness_name": "pi", "model": "stub/stub-model", "argv": ["pi", "--mode", "json", "--model", "stub/stub-model", "--", "Reply with exactly: pong"]}
{"type": "text", "text": "pong"}
{"type": "result", "harness_name": "pi", "model": "stub/stub-model", "text": "pong", "exit_code": 0, "is_error": false, "duration_ms": 1047, "session_id": "01a19507-07fe-7550-b76e-7a5f6b29a908", "usage": {"input_tokens": 11, "output_tokens": 2}, "cost_usd": 0, "argv": ["pi", "--mode", "json", "--model", "stub/stub-model", "--", "Reply with exactly: pong"]}
```

Each line is written and flushed as soon as it happens, so a reader sees progress live.

![Timeline of stream events: start, tool_use, tool_result, text, result, and how each harness's own stream maps onto them](../images/stream-events.svg)

There are five event types:

| `type` | When | Fields |
|---|---|---|
| `start` | Once, when the harness binary has been found | `harness_name`, `model`, `argv` |
| `text` | The assistant wrote text | `text` |
| `tool_use` | The model called a tool | `id`, `name`, `input` |
| `tool_result` | The tool returned | `id`, `is_error`, `output` |
| `result` | Always last | The same fields as `-o json` |

## A run with a tool call

When the agent uses a tool, you see the call, then its result, then the answer. This is claude
running a shell command:

```json
{"type": "start", "harness_name": "claude-code", "model": null, "argv": ["claude", "-p", "--output-format", "stream-json", "--verbose", "--", "Say hi."]}
{"type": "tool_use", "id": "toolu_stub_1", "name": "Bash", "input": {"command": "echo hi"}}
{"type": "tool_result", "id": "toolu_stub_1", "is_error": false, "output": "hi"}
{"type": "text", "text": "pong"}
{"type": "result", "harness_name": "claude-code", "text": "pong", "is_error": false, "…": "…"}
```

`name` and `input` are the harness's own tool name and arguments: `Bash` for claude,
`command_execution` for codex, `bash` for pi and opencode, `run_terminal_command` for grok.
`tool_result.id` matches the `tool_use` it answers. A refused or failed call has `"is_error": true`.

## What differs between harnesses

- `text` is a whole message for claude, codex and opencode, but pieces of a message for pi and grok.
  Join the `text` events in order to get everything the assistant said. The final answer is always
  `result.text`.
- callai switches claude to `--output-format stream-json --verbose` and grok to
  `--output-format streaming-json`. The other harnesses already stream.
- hermes has no event stream, so you get only `start` and `result`.

## When something goes wrong

- If the harness isn't installed, nothing is printed on stdout (not even `start`), and callai exits
  127.
- A failed run still ends with a `result` event with `is_error: true`.
- A timeout (124) or Ctrl-C (130) ends the stream without a `result`. The exit code says why.

## Recap

- `-o stream-json` = `start`, then `text` / `tool_use` / `tool_result` live, then `result`.
- Same events for every harness; `result` is the `-o json` object.
- No `result` line means callai itself stopped the run: check the exit code.

Reference: [Stream events](../reference/output.md#-o-stream-json) · Guide: [Build a live progress view](../guides/live-progress.md)

Next: [5. Continue a conversation](05-sessions.md) · Previous: [3. Control what the agent may do](03-permissions.md)

<!-- source: tutorial/05-sessions.md -->
# 5. Continue a conversation

Every run reports a `session_id`. Pass it to `--resume` to continue that conversation, or use
`--continue` for the harness's most recent one.

**You'll need:** [step 2](02-json-output.md).

## Resume by id

```bash
SID=$(callai -n claude-code -p "Reply with exactly: pong" -o json < /dev/null | jq -r .session_id)
callai -n claude-code -p "And again?" --resume "$SID" -o json < /dev/null | jq --arg sid "$SID" '.text, .session_id == $sid'
```

```text
"pong"
true
```

The second run carries the first run's turns: the model sees the whole conversation. The run reports
the same `session_id`.

`--dry-run` shows the harness's own flag:

```bash
callai -n claude-code -p "And again?" --resume SESSION_ID --dry-run
```

```text
claude -p --output-format json --resume SESSION_ID -- 'And again?'
```

Each harness spells it differently, and callai maps it for you:

| Harness | `--resume ID` | `--continue` |
|---|---|---|
| claude-code | `--resume ID` | `--continue` (most recent in this directory) |
| codex | `exec … resume ID -- PROMPT` | `exec … resume --last -- PROMPT` |
| opencode | `--session ID` | `--continue` |
| pi | `--session ID` | `--continue` |
| hermes | `--resume ID` | refused, see below |
| grok | `--resume=ID` | `--continue` (most recent for this directory) |

This was checked with each real harness: the resumed request contains the earlier turns.

## Continue the most recent session

```bash
callai -n codex -p "Now add a test for it" --continue
```

"Most recent" is the harness's own idea of it, which usually means the most recent in the current
directory. If several things use the same harness in the same place, prefer `--resume` with an id.

> [!NOTE]
> **hermes refuses `--continue`.** `hermes chat --continue` only looks at interactive sessions, never
> at the non-interactive ones callai starts, so it would continue a different conversation. Use
> `--resume` with the `session_id` callai reported:
>
> ```text
> callai: error: --continue: hermes only continues its most recent interactive session, not callai's runs; use --resume with the session_id callai reported
> ```

## Rules

- `--resume` and `--continue` can't be combined.
- There's no `-c` short form for `--continue`, because `-c` already means `--command` (the prompt).
- A session id can't start with `-`, because the harness would read it as an option.
- Permissions apply to every run, resumed or not. For codex, callai checked that a resumed run gets
  the sandbox you ask for this time.

## Recap

- `session_id` from `-o json` → `--resume ID` continues that conversation.
- `--continue` picks the harness's latest session (not for hermes).

Reference: [`--resume`](../reference/cli.md#--resume-session_id) · [`--continue`](../reference/cli.md#--continue)

Next: [6. Ask several harnesses at once](06-fan-out.md) · Previous: [4. Watch a run as it happens](04-streaming.md)

<!-- source: tutorial/06-fan-out.md -->
# 6. Ask several harnesses at once

Give `-n` several names to run one prompt through each of them. Separate the names with `/` to run
them at the same time, or with `,` to run them one after another. `-n all` runs every installed harness.

**You'll need:** [step 2](02-json-output.md), and two or more harnesses installed.

## At the same time

```bash
callai -n codex/pi/grok -p "Reply with exactly: pong"
```

```text
== codex ==
pong
== pi ==
pong
== grok ==
pong
```

The answers print in the order you named the harnesses, whichever finishes first, each under a
`== name ==` header.

![Fan-out timeline: with '/' the harnesses run at the same time and the call ends when the slowest does; with ',' they run one after another](../images/fan-out.svg)

## One after another

```bash
callai -n codex,pi,grok -p "Reply with exactly: pong"
```

The output looks the same. The difference is timing, and what the harnesses can see: they all share
one working directory, so use `,` for prompts that edit files. Otherwise two agents edit the same files
at once.

## Every installed harness

```bash
callai -n all -p "Reply with exactly: pong" --permission read-only
```

```text
callai: skipping opencode: --permission read-only: opencode has no read-only mode (its plan agent still allows shell commands); pass `-- --agent plan` yourself if that is acceptable
callai: skipping hermes: --permission read-only: hermes has no read-only toolset (its `file` toolset can write); use the default or --permission auto
== claude-code ==
pong
== codex ==
pong
== pi ==
pong
== grok ==
pong
```

`-n all` uses only the harnesses that are installed, and skips (with a note on stderr) any that can't
honour your options. With an explicit list, a harness that can't honour them stops the whole call
before anything runs.

## When one fails

```bash
callai -n claude-code/codex -m not-a-real-model-xyz -p hi
echo "exit=$?"
```

```text
== claude-code (failed, exit 1) ==
There's an issue with the selected model (not-a-real-model-xyz). It may not exist or you may not have access to it. Run --model to pick a different model.
== codex (failed, exit 1) ==
The model `not-a-real-model-xyz` does not exist.
exit=1
```

One failure doesn't stop the others. Each failed harness's own stderr follows on stderr under a
`--- name stderr ---` line. The exit code is 0 if every run succeeded, otherwise the first failure's in
the order given. A harness that times out becomes a failed result with exit code 124, and the others
keep going. Ctrl-C stops them all (exit 130).

## JSON and events

- `-o json` gives `{"results": [ … ]}`: one `-o json` object per harness, in order.
- `-o stream-json` interleaves the harnesses' events live. Every event carries `harness_name`.
- `--dry-run` prints one command line per harness. With `-o json` it prints `{"runs": [ … ]}`.

## Rules

- `-m` applies to every harness. Model names differ between harnesses, so give each its own with a
  [model alias](07-defaults.md#name-models-once-with-aliases), or leave `-m` out.
- Piped stdin is read once and shared.
- `-o raw` and arguments after `--` need a single harness, because they are specific to one harness.
- Mixing separators (`a/b,c`), repeating a name, or putting `all` in a list is a usage error.

## Recap

- `-n a/b/c` runs at the same time, `-n a,b,c` one after another, and `-n all` every installed harness.
- Results come back in the order given; the exit code is the first failure's.

Reference: [`-n`](../reference/cli.md#-n-harness_name---name-harness_name) · [Fan-out output](../reference/output.md#fan-out) · Guide: [Compare harnesses side by side](../guides/compare-harnesses.md)

Next: [7. Set your defaults](07-defaults.md) · Previous: [5. Continue a conversation](05-sessions.md)

<!-- source: tutorial/07-defaults.md -->
# 7. Set your defaults

Set a default harness, model and timeout once, in environment variables or a config file, and give
models short names that mean the right thing for each harness.

**You'll need:** [step 1](01-first-prompt.md).

## Environment variables

```bash
export CALLAI_HARNESS_NAME=codex
export CALLAI_TIMEOUT=600
callai -p "Reply with exactly: pong"          # runs codex, killed after 10 minutes
```

| Variable | Sets | Same as |
|---|---|---|
| `CALLAI_HARNESS_NAME` | Harness (also `a/b`, `a,b`, `all`) | `-n` |
| `CALLAI_MODEL` | Model or alias | `-m` |
| `CALLAI_TIMEOUT` | Seconds | `--timeout` |
| `CALLAI_STDIN_WAIT` | Seconds to wait for piped input with `-p` (default 3) | — |
| `CALLAI_CONFIG` | Path of the config file | — |

A flag always wins over its variable. An empty variable counts as unset.

## The config file

callai reads `~/.config/callai/config.toml` (or `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/callai/config.toml`, or the file
named in `CALLAI_CONFIG`). It is optional:

```toml
default_harness = "claude-code"
model = "fast"                       # default model for every harness (here an alias)
timeout = 600

[harnesses.codex]
model = "gpt-5-codex"                # codex's own default; beats the top-level model
extra_args = ["--ephemeral"]         # passed to codex before anything after --

[aliases]
fast  = { claude-code = "haiku", codex = "gpt-5-codex-mini", opencode = "anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5" }
smart = { claude-code = "opus",  codex = "gpt-5-codex" }
```

With that file:

```bash
callai -p "Explain main.py" --dry-run
callai -n codex -p "Explain main.py" --dry-run
callai -n codex -m smart -p "Explain main.py" --dry-run
CALLAI_MODEL=o3 callai -n codex -p "Explain main.py" --dry-run
```

```text
claude -p --output-format json --model haiku -- 'Explain main.py'
codex exec --json --skip-git-repo-check --model gpt-5-codex --ephemeral -- 'Explain main.py'
codex exec --json --skip-git-repo-check --model gpt-5-codex --ephemeral -- 'Explain main.py'
codex exec --json --skip-git-repo-check --model o3 --ephemeral -- 'Explain main.py'
```

Line by line:
1. No `-n`, so `default_harness` chose claude-code. The top-level `model = "fast"` resolved through
   the alias to `haiku`.
2. codex's own `[harnesses.codex] model` beat the top-level one, and its `extra_args` were added.
3. `-m smart` resolved to codex's entry in the `smart` alias, which is also `gpt-5-codex`.
4. `CALLAI_MODEL` beat the config, and `o3` isn't an alias, so it passed through unchanged.

## Precedence

![Precedence: command-line flag, then CALLAI_* environment variable, then the harness's config table, then the top-level config, then the harness's default; model aliases are resolved after](../images/precedence.svg)

The first source that sets a value wins:

1. command-line flag;
2. `CALLAI_*` environment variable;
3. `[harnesses.<name>]` in the config file (`model` only);
4. top level of the config file;
5. the harness's own default.

Model aliases are resolved after that.

## Name models once with aliases

An alias maps one name to a model per harness. `-m fast` means `haiku` for claude-code and
`gpt-5-codex-mini` for codex. That is what makes `-m` useful with [fan-out](06-fan-out.md). A model that
isn't an alias goes to the harness unchanged. An alias with no entry for the harness you're running is
an error, so a wrong model is never sent:

```text
callai: error: model alias 'smart' has no entry for pi
```

## Typos are errors

Unknown keys, unknown harness names and wrong types stop callai with exit 2, naming the file:

```text
callai: error: /home/me/.config/callai/config.toml: unknown key 'defualt_harness'; allowed: aliases, default_harness, harnesses, model, timeout
```

## Recap

- Defaults come from flag › environment › config file › harness default.
- `[harnesses.<name>]` sets a per-harness `binary`, `model` and `extra_args`.
- `[aliases]` give one model name a meaning per harness.

Reference: [Configuration](../reference/configuration.md)

Next: [8. Use callai from Python](08-python-api.md) · Previous: [6. Ask several harnesses at once](06-fan-out.md)

<!-- source: tutorial/08-python-api.md -->
# 8. Use callai from Python

`callai.run()` runs a harness from Python and returns the same result as `-o json`. An optional
callback receives the stream events as they happen.

**You'll need:** callai installed in your Python environment ([Installation](../getting-started/installation.md)).

## Run and read the result

```python
import callai

result = callai.run("claude-code", "Reply with exactly: pong")
print(result.text, result.is_error, result.exit_code)
print(result.session_id is not None, result.usage)
```

```text
pong False 0
True {'input_tokens': 11, 'output_tokens': 2}
```

`result` is a frozen `callai.Result` with the same fields as the `-o json` object. `result.to_dict()`
gives that object.

## Pass options

The CLI's options become keyword arguments:

```python
result = callai.run(
    "codex",
    "Fix the failing test",
    model="gpt-5-codex",
    cwd="/path/to/repo",
    timeout=600,
    permission="auto",
    system_prompt="Keep changes minimal.",
    extra_args=["--ephemeral"],
)
```

## Continue the conversation

```python
again = callai.run("claude-code", "And again?", resume=result.session_id)
print(again.session_id == result.session_id)
```

```text
True
```

## Watch events

```python
import callai

def show(event):
    print(event["type"], event.get("text", ""))

callai.run("codex", "Reply with exactly: pong", on_event=show)
```

```text
start 
text pong
result pong
```

`on_event` receives the same dicts that `-o stream-json` prints, in order, from a background thread.
With it, the harness runs in its streaming mode.

## Handle failures

A harness that runs but fails returns a result with `is_error=True`. An exception means the run
couldn't start or finish:

```python
import callai

try:
    callai.run("codex", "hi", binary="/nonexistent/codex")
except callai.HarnessNotFound as exc:
    print("not installed:", exc)

result = callai.run("claude-code", "hi", model="not-a-real-model-xyz")
print(result.is_error, result.exit_code)
```

```text
not installed: harness binary '/nonexistent/codex' not found on PATH (needed for --name codex); install it: https://developers.openai.com/codex/cli
True 1
```

| Exception | When |
|---|---|
| `callai.UsageError` | Bad argument, or an option the harness can't honour |
| `callai.HarnessNotFound` | The binary isn't on `PATH` |
| `callai.HarnessTimeout` | `timeout` expired; the harness was killed |
| `callai.Interrupted` | Ctrl-C |

All four are subclasses of `callai.CallaiError`.

## Differences from the CLI

`callai.run()` ignores `CALLAI_*` environment variables and the config file, so a call does the same
thing on every machine. Pass everything explicitly. Model aliases are a CLI feature: `model=` is sent
as is. Use `binary=` to run a specific executable.

## Recap

- `callai.run(harness, prompt, **options)` → `Result`, the same as `-o json`.
- `on_event=` receives stream events; `resume=` continues a session.
- Failed runs are results; exceptions mean the run couldn't happen.

Reference: [Python API](../reference/python-api.md)

Previous: [7. Set your defaults](07-defaults.md) · Up: [Tutorial](README.md) · Next: [How-to guides](../guides/README.md)

# How-to guides

Task-focused recipes. Each one stands alone, so read them in any order. They assume you know the basics
from the [Tutorial](../tutorial/README.md).

- [Call callai from an AI agent](use-from-an-ai-agent.md): run harnesses as sub-agents safely and parse what comes back.
- [Use callai in scripts and CI](scripts-and-ci.md): stdin, timeouts, exit codes and JSON in shell pipelines.
- [Compare harnesses side by side](compare-harnesses.md): one prompt, every harness, a model alias each.
- [Build a live progress view](live-progress.md): turn stream events into a progress display.
- [Test without a real model](test-without-a-model.md): fake harnesses for your tests, and real harnesses against a stub model.
- [Add a new harness](add-a-harness.md): write an adapter and prove it with the conformance suite.

<!-- source: guides/use-from-an-ai-agent.md -->
# How to call callai from an AI agent

Use this when an agent or orchestrator hands work to another coding agent (a "sub-agent") and needs a
reliable answer and status back.

## The safe invocation

```bash
callai -n codex -p "TASK" -o json --permission read-only --timeout 600 -C /path/to/repo < /dev/null
```

| Part | Why |
|---|---|
| `-o json` | One object to parse: `text`, `is_error`, `exit_code`, `session_id`. |
| `--permission read-only` | Choose the level explicitly. The default is the harness's own, which for opencode, pi and hermes already allows writes and shell. Use `auto` when the sub-agent should edit files. |
| `--timeout 600` | A stuck harness is killed, with everything it started (exit 124). |
| `-C /path/to/repo` | The directory the sub-agent works in. |
| `< /dev/null` | Your agent's stdin may be an open, silent pipe. callai would otherwise wait 3 seconds for it, then warn. |

## Decide what happened

Branch on the exit code first, then on the JSON:

| Exit code | Meaning | What the agent should do |
|---|---|---|
| `0` | Success | Use `text`. |
| `2` | Usage error; nothing ran | Read stderr. Fix the call (e.g. that harness can't do `read-only`). Don't retry as is. |
| `124` | Timed out | Retry with a longer `--timeout` or a smaller task. |
| `127` | Harness not installed | Pick another harness (`callai --list-harnesses -o json`). |
| `130` | Interrupted | Stop. |
| other | The harness failed | `is_error` is true. `text` is the reason (e.g. a bad model name). |

## From Python

```python
import json
import subprocess

proc = subprocess.run(
    ["callai", "-n", "codex", "-p", "Reply with exactly: pong", "-o", "json",
     "--permission", "read-only", "--timeout", "600"],
    stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL, capture_output=True, text=True,
)
if proc.returncode == 2:
    raise ValueError(proc.stderr.strip().splitlines()[-1])   # the "callai: error: ..." line
result = json.loads(proc.stdout) if proc.stdout else None
print(proc.returncode, result and result["text"])
```

```text
0 pong
```

Or skip the subprocess and use [`callai.run()`](../reference/python-api.md), which raises `UsageError`,
`HarnessNotFound` or `HarnessTimeout` instead of returning those exit codes.

## Patterns

**Keep a sub-agent's context across steps:** save `session_id` and pass `--resume`:

```bash
callai -n claude-code -p "Read src/ and summarise the architecture" -o json < /dev/null > step1.json
callai -n claude-code -p "Now list the riskiest module" --resume "$(jq -r .session_id step1.json)" -o json < /dev/null
```

**Get a second opinion:** run several harnesses on the same question and compare the answers:

```bash
callai -n claude-code/codex -p "Is this migration safe? $(cat migration.sql)" -o json < /dev/null \
  | jq -r '.results[] | "\(.harness_name): \(.text)"'
```

**Follow long runs:** use `-o stream-json` and read line by line; see
[Build a live progress view](live-progress.md).

## Instructions to give your agent

Paste this into the agent's instructions (e.g. `AGENTS.md` or `CLAUDE.md`) and adjust the harnesses and
levels:

```markdown
## Delegating to other coding agents

Use `callai` to run a prompt through another coding agent:

    callai -n <claude-code|codex|opencode|pi|hermes|grok> -p "<task>" -o json --permission <read-only|auto> --timeout 900 -C <dir> < /dev/null

- Parse stdout as JSON: `text` is the answer, `is_error` says whether it failed, `session_id` continues
  the conversation with `--resume <id>`.
- Exit 2 means the call was invalid and nothing ran: read stderr and fix the call. 124 = timed out,
  127 = harness not installed.
- Never use `--permission bypass` unless the user asked for it.
- `callai --dry-run ...` shows the exact command without running it.
```

## Troubleshooting

- **It waits 3 seconds before starting:** stdin is an open pipe. Add `< /dev/null`, or set
  `CALLAI_STDIN_WAIT=0`.
- **`--permission read-only` is refused:** opencode and hermes have no read-only mode. Pick another
  harness, or accept their default knowingly.
- **The answer is empty and `is_error` is true:** read `text` (the harness's error) and callai's
  stderr, where the harness's own stderr is copied on failure.

See also: [Use callai in scripts and CI](scripts-and-ci.md) · [Exit codes and errors](../reference/errors.md) · [Permissions](../concepts/permissions.md)

<!-- source: guides/scripts-and-ci.md -->
# How to use callai in scripts and CI

Use this when a shell script or CI job calls a coding agent and must handle every outcome.

## A robust script

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -uo pipefail

out=$(callai -n codex -p "Reply with exactly: pong" -o json --timeout 900 < /dev/null)
code=$?

case $code in
  0)   jq -r .text <<<"$out" ;;
  2)   echo "callai usage error (nothing ran)" >&2; exit 2 ;;
  124) echo "agent timed out" >&2; exit 1 ;;
  127) echo "harness not installed" >&2; exit 1 ;;
  *)   echo "agent failed: $(jq -r .text <<<"$out")" >&2; exit 1 ;;
esac
```

```text
pong
```

- **No `set -e`:** the script needs to see callai's exit code, not stop on it.
- **`< /dev/null`:** CI runners often give jobs an open stdin. Without the redirect, callai waits 3
  seconds for input, then warns and carries on.
- **`--timeout`:** a stuck harness and everything it started are killed (exit 124), so the job doesn't
  hang until the CI limit.

## Feed files and diffs in

```bash
echo "def add(a, b): return a - b" | callai -n codex -p "Review this code" --dry-run
```

```text
codex exec --json --skip-git-repo-check -- 'Review this code

def add(a, b): return a - b'
```

Piped stdin is appended to the `-p` prompt after a blank line. To use only stdin as the prompt, use
`-p -` or leave `-p` out; callai then waits for the pipe to close, however long that takes.

## Keep the answer and the logs apart

- stdout has the answer (or the JSON).
- stderr has callai's warnings and errors, plus the harness's stderr when it fails.
- `-v` copies the harness's stderr live on every run, which is useful in CI logs.

```bash
callai -n codex -p "…" -o json -v < /dev/null > result.json 2> agent.log
```

## Pin the behaviour

- Use `--permission` explicitly in CI. `read-only` for review jobs, `auto` for fix-up jobs.
- Set the model with `-m`, or with a config file committed to the repo and selected through
  `CALLAI_CONFIG=ci/callai.toml`. An unknown key in that file fails the job (exit 2) instead of being
  ignored.
- `callai --dry-run …` in a CI step prints the exact harness command for the log.

## Credentials

callai never handles credentials: each harness reads its own (`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`,
`XAI_API_KEY`, a signed-in config, …). Provide them to the job the way that harness documents.

See also: [Call callai from an AI agent](use-from-an-ai-agent.md) · [Exit codes and errors](../reference/errors.md) · [Configuration](../reference/configuration.md)

<!-- source: guides/compare-harnesses.md -->
# How to compare harnesses side by side

Use this to ask several coding agents the same question and compare their answers, speed and token use.

## 1. Give each harness a model under one name

Model names differ per harness, so define an alias in `~/.config/callai/config.toml`:

```toml
[aliases]
best = { claude-code = "opus", codex = "gpt-5-codex", opencode = "anthropic/claude-opus-4-1", pi = "anthropic/claude-opus-4-1", hermes = "anthropic/claude-opus-4-1", grok = "grok-4" }
```

Now `-m best` means the right model for each. An alias missing an entry for one of the harnesses in
your run is an error, so you notice before anything runs.

## 2. Run them all at once

```bash
callai -n all -m best -p "Explain what src/main.py does in two sentences" -o json --permission read-only < /dev/null > compare.json
```

`-n all` runs every installed harness at the same time and skips those that can't honour
`--permission read-only` (opencode and hermes), saying so on stderr. To choose exactly which harnesses
run, list them instead: `-n claude-code/codex/grok`.

## 3. Tabulate

```bash
jq -r '.results[] | [.harness_name, (if .is_error then "FAILED" else "ok" end), .duration_ms, (.usage.input_tokens // "-"), (.usage.output_tokens // "-")] | @tsv' compare.json
```

```text
claude-code	ok	932	11	2
codex	ok	298	11	2
pi	ok	545	11	2
grok	ok	523	11	2
```

The columns are harness, status, duration in ms, input tokens and output tokens. Pipe through
`column -t` to align them. These numbers come from the stub model, so yours will be much larger.

And the answers:

```bash
jq -r '.results[] | "## \(.harness_name)\n\(.text)\n"' compare.json
```

## Variations

- **Same harness, several models:** run one command per model. `-n` lists harnesses, not models.
- **Watch them work:** `-o stream-json` interleaves every harness's events live, each tagged with
  `harness_name`.
- **Files may change:** harnesses that edit files share one working directory. Run them one after
  another (`-n claude-code,codex`) and reset the tree between runs, or give each its own clone with
  separate commands using `-C`.

See also: [6. Ask several harnesses at once](../tutorial/06-fan-out.md) · [Model aliases](../reference/configuration.md#aliases)

<!-- source: guides/live-progress.md -->
# How to build a live progress view

Use this to show what a coding agent is doing while it works: tool calls, their results and its
messages. It works for a terminal, a log or a UI.

## From Python, with `on_event`

```python
import callai


def show(event):
    kind = event["type"]
    if kind == "start":
        print(f"▶ {event['harness_name']} started")
    elif kind == "tool_use":
        print(f"  ⚙ {event['name']} {event['input']}")
    elif kind == "tool_result":
        status = "✗" if event["is_error"] else "✓"
        print(f"  {status} {event['output'][:60]!r}")
    elif kind == "text":
        print(f"  💬 {event['text']}")
    elif kind == "result":
        print(f"■ done in {event['duration_ms']} ms, error={event['is_error']}")


result = callai.run("claude-code", "Say hi.", permission="bypass", on_event=show)
```

```text
▶ claude-code started
  ⚙ Bash {'command': 'echo hi'}
  ✓ 'hi'
  💬 pong
■ done in 834 ms, error=False
```

The callback runs on a background thread, once per event, in order. Keep it quick, or hand events to
a queue.

## From any language, with `-o stream-json`

Read stdout line by line. Each line is one JSON object, flushed as it happens:

```python
import json
import subprocess

proc = subprocess.Popen(
    ["callai", "-n", "codex", "-p", "Reply with exactly: pong", "-o", "stream-json"],
    stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, text=True,
)
for line in proc.stdout:
    event = json.loads(line)
    print(event["type"], event.get("text", ""))
proc.wait()
print("exit", proc.returncode)
```

```text
start 
text pong
result pong
exit 0
```

## Things to handle

- **Text arrives in pieces for some harnesses** (pi, grok) and as whole messages for others. Append
  `text` events as they arrive; the final answer is in the `result` event.
- **hermes has no event stream:** you get `start` and `result` only.
- **No `result` event:** callai stopped the run (timeout 124, Ctrl-C 130). Use the exit code.
- **Several harnesses:** with `-n a/b`, events from all of them interleave. Group by `harness_name`,
  which every event carries in fan-out mode.

See also: [4. Watch a run as it happens](../tutorial/04-streaming.md) · [Stream events reference](../reference/output.md#-o-stream-json)

<!-- source: guides/test-without-a-model.md -->
# How to test without a real model

Use this to test code that calls callai without spending tokens or needing network access. There are
two levels, depending on what you need to be real.

## Level 1: a fake harness binary

Your tests don't need a harness at all, just something that prints what a harness prints. Point callai
at a script that replays recorded output:

```bash
cat > fake-codex <<'EOF'
#!/bin/sh
cat <<'OUT'
{"type":"thread.started","thread_id":"t-1"}
{"type":"item.completed","item":{"id":"item_0","type":"agent_message","text":"pong"}}
{"type":"turn.completed","usage":{"input_tokens":11,"output_tokens":2}}
OUT
EOF
chmod +x fake-codex
```

```python
import callai

result = callai.run("codex", "anything", binary="./fake-codex")
print(result.text, result.session_id, result.usage)
```

```text
pong t-1 {'input_tokens': 11, 'output_tokens': 2}
```

From the CLI, set the binary in a test config file:

```toml
# test-callai.toml, used with CALLAI_CONFIG=test-callai.toml
[harnesses.codex]
binary = "./fake-codex"
```

Real recorded outputs for every harness, including failures, are in
[`conformance/parse/`](../../../conformance/parse/). Replaying one tests your code against exactly what
that harness prints.

## Level 2: real harnesses, stub model

To test the harness too (its flags, tools and permissions), keep the real harness CLI and replace only
the model. [`conformance/tools/stub_llm_server.py`](../../../conformance/tools/stub_llm_server.py) is a
local stub that speaks the OpenAI Responses, OpenAI Chat Completions and Anthropic Messages APIs:

```bash
python3 conformance/tools/stub_llm_server.py --port 8765 --reply pong
```

Then point each harness at `http://127.0.0.1:8765`. For example, claude:

```bash
ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8765 ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=stub callai -n claude-code -m stub-model -p "Say hi."
```

```text
pong
```

The other harnesses are configured through their provider settings. The exact settings for codex,
opencode, pi, hermes and grok are in the
[conformance README](../../../conformance/README.md), under "Recording without network or API keys".

The stub can also script a tool call, so you can test what a permission level really allows:

```bash
python3 conformance/tools/stub_llm_server.py --port 8765 \
  --tool-call '{"name": "Bash", "arguments": {"command": "echo hi"}}'
```

The stub returns that call to the first request that offers tools, and plain text once the harness
sends the tool's result back. It replies with text, not a new tool call, to any request that already
contains a tool result.

> [!TIP]
> Run claude against the stub with a clean environment (`env -i PATH="$PATH" HOME=…`), so your own
> `ANTHROPIC_*` or `CLAUDE_*` variables don't leak in.

See also: [Use callai in scripts and CI](scripts-and-ci.md) · [Python API](../reference/python-api.md)

<!-- source: guides/add-a-harness.md -->
# How to add a new harness

Use this to teach callai a new coding-agent CLI. An adapter is one Python file with a few pure
functions, plus conformance cases that prove it matches the real CLI.

## 1. Learn the CLI from the CLI

Read its `--help`. Docs and memory are hints; `--help` and real output are the truth. Find:

- how to run one prompt non-interactively, and how to stop the prompt being read as a flag (`--`, or
  one `--opt=PROMPT` argument);
- its structured output mode (JSON, or JSON lines);
- its model flag, permission or sandbox flags, system-prompt option, and session resume flags;
- whether it reads stdin (callai gives it an empty one) and how it reports failure.

## 2. Write the adapter

Create `src/callai/adapters/<name>.py`:

```python
from ..request import Request
from ..result import Completed, Result
from .base import Adapter


class MyAgent(Adapter):
    name = "my-agent"                       # the -n value
    binary = "myagent"                      # looked up on PATH
    install_url = "https://example.com/install"

    def build_argv(self, req: Request) -> list[str]:
        argv = [self.binary, "run", "--json"]
        if req.model:
            argv += ["--model", req.model]
        return [*argv, *req.extra_args, "--", req.prompt]   # prompt last, after --

    def parse(self, completed: Completed, req: Request) -> Result:
        ...                                  # turn stdout into a Result
```

| Method | Required | Job |
|---|---|---|
| `build_argv(req)` | yes | The exact command line. Raise `UsageError` for anything the CLI can't honour (fail closed). |
| `parse(completed, req)` | yes | Stdout/stderr/exit code → `Result`. Take `is_error` from the CLI's own error signal. |
| `stream_events(line, state)` | for `-o stream-json` | One stdout line → `text` / `tool_use` / `tool_result` events. |
| `build_env(req)` | if needed | Environment variables, for settings the CLI only takes that way. |

All four are pure: no I/O. That's what lets `--dry-run` and the tests work without the CLI installed.
Map each `--permission` level to the CLI's flags, then prove it in step 4.

## 3. Register it

In `src/callai/adapters/__init__.py`, add the name to `HARNESS_NAMES` and register an instance next to
the others:

```python
from .my_agent import MyAgent  # noqa: E402

register(MyAgent())
```

## 4. Prove it with the conformance suite

The suite in [`conformance/`](../../../conformance/README.md) is plain JSON, shared by every
implementation of callai:

- `argv/<name>/*.json`: request → the exact argv (or the expected refusal);
- `parse/<name>/*.json` + recorded stdout/stderr: real output → the expected `Result` fields, and
  optionally `expected_events`;
- `cli/*.json`: end-to-end cases that replay recorded output through a fake binary.

Record the parse fixtures from the real CLI. Without network access or API keys, run it against the
[stub model](test-without-a-model.md#level-2-real-harnesses-stub-model) and label the fixture
"STUB MODEL". Then check every permission level with
`python conformance/tools/permission_probe.py --name <name> --model <model> --outside <dir>`, which
runs scripted writes and shell commands and reports what really happened.

## 5. Document it

Add the harness to [Harnesses](../reference/harnesses.md), the permission table in
[Permissions](../concepts/permissions.md), and the install table in
[Installation](../getting-started/installation.md).

See also: [Architecture](../concepts/architecture.md) · [Harnesses reference](../reference/harnesses.md)

<!-- source: concepts/README.md -->
# Concepts

How callai works and why it behaves as it does. Read these when you want the reasoning; the
[Reference](../reference/README.md) has the exact contracts.

- [Architecture](architecture.md): adapters, the runner, and the one run path the CLI and the API share.
- [Permissions](permissions.md): what each level allows per harness, and why callai fails closed.
- [Normalised output](normalised-output.md): how six output formats become one result and one event stream.

## Glossary

| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **harness** | A coding-agent CLI that callai drives: `claude-code`, `codex`, `opencode`, `pi`, `hermes`, `grok`. Chosen with `-n`. |
| **harness name** | The `-n` value (`claude-code`), which isn't always the binary name (`claude`). |
| **adapter** | The callai module for one harness. It turns a request into that harness's command line and the harness's output into a result. |
| **request** | Everything about one run: harness, prompt, model, permission, session, extra args. |
| **result** | The normalised outcome: the `-o json` object, or a `callai.Result` in Python. |
| **event** | One line of `-o stream-json`: `start`, `text`, `tool_use`, `tool_result` or `result`. |
| **permission level** | `default`, `read-only`, `auto` or `bypass`; translated per harness. |
| **session** | A harness conversation, identified by `session_id`, that `--resume` continues. |
| **fan-out** | One prompt through several harnesses: `-n a/b` (at the same time), `-n a,b` (one after another), `-n all`. |
| **model alias** | A config name (`fast`) that maps to a different model per harness. |
| **fail closed** | Refusing (exit 2) rather than running with more access than asked for, or silently ignoring an option. |
| **stub model** | `conformance/tools/stub_llm_server.py`: a local fake model API for testing real harnesses offline. |

<!-- source: concepts/architecture.md -->
# Architecture

callai is a thin translator. One adapter per harness builds the command line and reads the output back,
and a single runner runs everything, for both the CLI and the Python API.

![Architecture: the CLI and the Python API both create a Request; the harness's Adapter builds argv and env; runner.run executes the harness CLI in its own process group; the same Adapter turns stdout into stream events and a Result, which is printed or returned](../images/architecture.svg)

The same flow in words:

1. **Entry:** the CLI resolves flags, `CALLAI_*` variables and `config.toml`. The Python API takes
   keyword arguments only. Both produce a `Request`, one per harness when fanning out.
2. **Build:** the harness's adapter turns the request into a command line (`build_argv`) and any
   environment variables (`build_env`). It does no I/O, which is why `--dry-run` can print the command
   without the harness installed.
3. **Run:** `runner.run` finds the binary on `PATH` and starts it in its own process group, with an
   empty stdin. It reads stdout line by line as it arrives. On timeout it kills the whole group (exit
   124); on Ctrl-C it sends SIGINT to the group (exit 130).
4. **Read:** the same adapter turns each stdout line into stream events (`stream_events`) and the
   finished output into a `Result` (`parse`).
5. **Out:** the CLI prints text, JSON or stream events; the API returns the `Result`. `-o raw` skips
   step 4 and prints the harness's own output.

## The run, step by step

![The life of one run: resolve settings, check options, read the prompt, build, find the binary, run, parse, print; with the exit code each step can stop with](../images/run-lifecycle.svg)

| Step | Can stop with |
|---|---|
| 1. Resolve settings (flag › env › config › default) | exit 2: no harness, bad config, unknown flag |
| 2. Check the options the harness can't honour, **before reading stdin** | exit 2 |
| 3. Read the prompt (`-p`, plus piped stdin; 3 s wait on an idle pipe) | exit 2: no prompt |
| 4. Build argv and env | `--dry-run` prints here, exit 0 |
| 5. Find the binary | exit 127 |
| 6. Run | exit 124 (timeout), 130 (Ctrl-C) |
| 7. Parse | — |
| 8. Print | the harness's exit code, or 1 if it failed but exited 0 |

Step 2 comes before step 3 so that an impossible request fails at once, instead of after waiting for
a slow pipe.

## Why it's built this way

- **One adapter file per harness, pure functions.** Adapters are tested without any harness installed.
  A shared, language-agnostic [conformance suite](../../../conformance/README.md) pins their behaviour,
  and later ports (TypeScript, Rust) will run the same suite.
- **Always ask for structured output.** callai runs `claude --output-format json` even for `-o text`.
  The answer is taken from structured data, never scraped from a terminal display. hermes has no JSON
  mode, so its adapter strips the display lines instead.
- **The prompt is always last** (after `--`, or as one `--opt=PROMPT` argument), so a prompt can't be
  read as a flag.
- **Empty stdin for the harness.** Some harnesses read stdin when it isn't a terminal. callai reads
  stdin itself (into the prompt), so the harness gets an empty one.
- **No runtime dependencies.** Standard library only: fast start-up and easy installation.

## Code map

| Module | Role |
|---|---|
| `callai/cli.py` | Flags, defaults, rendering, exit codes |
| `callai/api.py` | `run()`, and `run_harness()`, the one run path |
| `callai/fanout.py` | `-n a/b`, `-n a,b`, `-n all` |
| `callai/runner.py` | Subprocess, process groups, timeouts, live output |
| `callai/config.py` | `config.toml`, aliases |
| `callai/request.py`, `result.py`, `errors.py` | The data types |
| `callai/adapters/*.py` | One per harness, plus `base.py` |

See also: [Add a new harness](../guides/add-a-harness.md) · [Harnesses reference](../reference/harnesses.md) · [Design notes](../../DESIGN.md)

<!-- source: concepts/permissions.md -->
# Permissions

`--permission` gives every harness the same four levels, maps each to that harness's own controls,
and refuses any level a harness can't honour.

## The levels

| Level | Intent | What callai adds |
|---|---|---|
| `default` | The harness's own default | Nothing |
| `read-only` | Read and search, no writes, no shell | The harness's read-only mode or a read-only tool list |
| `auto` | Edit files in the working directory without asking | Its "accept edits" mode, sandbox or a file-tool list |
| `bypass` | Run every tool call without asking | Its "skip all permissions" flag, with a warning on stderr |

## Verified behaviour

Each cell was checked by running the real harness against a stub model that asked it to write a file
and run a shell command, both inside and outside the working directory, and observing what happened:

| Level | claude-code | codex | opencode | pi | grok | hermes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `read-only` | plan mode: no writes, no shell | read-only sandbox | **refused** | read tools only | read tools only | **refused** |
| `auto` | edits inside the workspace | writes inside the workspace (sandboxed shell) | **refused** | file writes/edits, no shell | file writes/edits, no shell | file writes/edits, no shell |
| `bypass` | everything | everything | everything | everything | everything | everything |

The flags behind each cell are in the [Harnesses reference](../reference/harnesses.md).

## The default isn't the same everywhere

With `default`, **opencode, pi and hermes write files and run shell commands without asking**.
claude-code, codex and grok ask, and since no one is there to answer, the call is refused. A refused
tool call doesn't fail the run: the model is told the tool was refused and carries on. For unattended
runs, always choose a level explicitly.

## Failing closed

When a harness has no way to honour a level, callai refuses with exit 2 before running anything:

- **opencode** has no read-only mode: its `plan` agent still allows shell commands. It has no
  "accept edits only" mode either: `--auto` approves everything.
- **hermes** has no read-only toolset: its `file` toolset can write.

The error message tells you what the harness *can* do (e.g. `-- --agent plan` for opencode), so you
can choose it deliberately. The same rule covers other options: a `--system-prompt` that opencode
can't take, or a `--continue` that hermes would apply to the wrong session.

## grok and the working directory

callai's `auto` for grok allows file writes and edits but no shell. grok writes them **anywhere** the
user can write, not just in the working directory. (codex's `auto` is sandboxed to the workspace.)

callai doesn't add grok's sandbox automatically. On Linux it needs
[bubblewrap](https://github.com/containers/bubblewrap), and grok refuses to start without it, so adding it
would break `auto` on machines that don't have it. Opt in:

```bash
sudo apt install -y bubblewrap                                                # Linux, once
callai -n grok -p "Fix the failing test" --permission auto -- --sandbox workspace
GROK_SANDBOX=workspace callai -n grok -p "Fix the failing test" --permission auto
```

All of grok's sandbox profiles, `read-only` and `strict` included, still allow writes inside the
working directory. Use callai's `--permission read-only` when you need read-only.

## Running as root

claude refuses `bypass` when run as root, unless `IS_SANDBOX=1` is set. callai never sets it for you:
setting it is your decision about your environment.

See also: [3. Control what the agent may do](../tutorial/03-permissions.md) · [`--permission` reference](../reference/cli.md#--permission-level)

<!-- source: concepts/normalised-output.md -->
# Normalised output

Every harness reports its answer, errors, session and token use differently. callai maps them all onto
one result and one event stream, so code that reads callai's output works with any harness.

## One result

| Harness | Native output | Where the answer is | Error signal |
|---|---|---|---|
| claude-code | one JSON object | `result` | `is_error`, which can be true while `subtype` says `"success"` |
| codex | JSON lines | the last `agent_message` item | a `turn.failed` event |
| opencode | JSON lines | the text of the last step (earlier steps come before tool calls) | an `error` event or a non-zero exit; the reason is taken from stderr's ERROR log line |
| pi | JSON lines | the last assistant message | `stopReason` of `error`, `aborted` or `length` (pi exits 0 even then) |
| grok | one JSON object | `text` | `{"type": "error"}`, or `stopReason` other than `end_turn` |
| hermes | plain text | stdout minus its display lines (those end in `\r\n`) | a non-zero exit, or no answer |

callai's result has the same keys whichever harness answered. A value the harness doesn't report is
`null` rather than left out. See the [output reference](../reference/output.md#-o-json) for every field.

## Rules that make results comparable

- **`is_error` comes from the harness's explicit error signal**, never from a status word that can
  disagree with it.
- **`usage.input_tokens` counts every prompt token, cache reads and writes included.** codex already
  counts them that way. For claude, opencode, pi and grok, callai adds the cache counts back in, so the
  numbers compare across harnesses.
- **`model` is the model the harness says it used** (claude, pi, grok report it), otherwise the one
  you asked for.
- **`exit_code` is the harness's own.** callai's process exits with it, or with 1 when the harness
  reported an error but exited 0.

## One event stream

`-o stream-json` maps each harness's native stream onto five event types:

![How each harness's stream maps onto callai's start, tool_use, tool_result, text and result events](../images/stream-events.svg)

| callai event | claude | codex | opencode | pi | grok |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `text` | assistant `text` block | `agent_message` item | `text` part | `text_delta` | `text` |
| `tool_use` | assistant `tool_use` block | `item.started` | `tool_use` part | `tool_execution_start` | `tool_call` |
| `tool_result` | user `tool_result` block | `item.completed` | the same `tool_use` part, once finished | `tool_execution_end` | `tool_call_update` (completed or failed) |

hermes has no event stream, so it gives only `start` and `result`. callai writes `start` and `result`
itself; the adapters produce the rest.

## What isn't normalised

- **Tool names and inputs** are the harness's own (`Bash` and `{"command": …}` for claude,
  `command_execution` for codex). Mapping them onto a common set would hide real differences.
- **The text granularity** of events: whole messages for some harnesses, pieces for others.
- **`-o raw`**, which is the harness's output, byte for byte.

See also: [Output formats reference](../reference/output.md) · [Architecture](architecture.md)
