# Reference

The complete, exact contracts, one page per surface. Look things up here. To learn, start with the
[Tutorial](../tutorial/README.md).

- [Command line](cli.md): every flag of `callai`, with defaults and examples.
- [Python API](python-api.md): `callai.run()`, `Result` and the exceptions.
- [Output formats](output.md): text, JSON, stream events, raw, dry run, `--list-harnesses` and fan-out shapes.
- [Configuration](configuration.md): `config.toml`, environment variables and precedence.
- [Harnesses](harnesses.md): exactly how callai invokes each harness, and what each supports.
- [Exit codes and errors](errors.md): every exit code and error message, with its cause and fix.

<!-- source: reference/cli.md -->
# Command line reference

Every flag `callai` accepts. This page is exhaustive; for a gentler introduction see the
[Tutorial](../tutorial/README.md).

```text
callai -n HARNESS_NAME -p PROMPT [-m MODEL] [-o {text,json,stream-json,raw}] [-C CWD]
       [--timeout SECS] [--permission {default,read-only,auto,bypass}] [--system-prompt S]
       [--resume SESSION_ID | --continue] [--dry-run] [-v] [-- HARNESS_ARGS...]
callai --list-harnesses [-o json]
callai --version | --help
```

## Choosing the harness and prompt

### `-n HARNESS_NAME`, `--name HARNESS_NAME`

The harness to run: `claude-code`, `codex`, `opencode`, `pi`, `hermes` or `grok`. For several at once
(fan-out):

| Value | Runs |
|---|---|
| `codex` | one harness |
| `codex/pi/grok` | all of them at the same time |
| `codex,pi,grok` | all of them, one after another |
| `all` | every installed harness, at the same time; harnesses that refuse the options are skipped with a note |

Default: `CALLAI_HARNESS_NAME`, then `default_harness` in the config file. Neither set and no `-n`:
exit 2. Mixed separators, empty or repeated names, and `all` inside a list are usage errors.
[Fan-out output](output.md#fan-out).

### `-p PROMPT`, `--prompt PROMPT`

The prompt. `-c` and `--command` are aliases.

| Form | Prompt |
|---|---|
| `-p TEXT` | `TEXT`. Piped stdin, if any, is appended after a blank line. |
| `-p TEXT` with an idle stdin pipe | `TEXT`, after waiting `CALLAI_STDIN_WAIT` seconds (default 3) for input, then a warning. |
| `-p -` | stdin, read until it closes. |
| no `-p`, piped stdin | stdin, read until it closes. |

Empty stdin counts as no input. No prompt at all: exit 2. The prompt always reaches the harness as one
final argument, after `--` or as `--opt=PROMPT`, so it can't be read as a flag. grok prompts starting
with `/` and pi prompts starting with `@` are refused, because those harnesses would run or attach
them instead of sending them.

## Model and output

### `-m MODEL`, `--model MODEL`

Model passed to the harness verbatim, unless it's an [alias](configuration.md#aliases) in the config
file. Each harness has its own names (opencode and pi: `provider/model`). Default: `CALLAI_MODEL`, then
`[harnesses.<name>] model`, then the top-level `model`, then the harness's own default.

### `-o FORMAT`, `--output-format FORMAT`

| Value | Prints |
|---|---|
| `text` (default) | The answer only. On failure, the harness's stderr and the error go to stderr. |
| `json` | One normalised result object. [Schema](output.md#-o-json). |
| `stream-json` | One event per line, as it happens. [Events](output.md#-o-stream-json). |
| `raw` | The harness's own stdout and stderr, unchanged. Single harness only. |

## Where and how long

### `-C CWD`, `--cwd CWD`

Working directory for the harness. Default: the current directory. Not a directory: exit 2.

### `--timeout SECS`

Kill the harness, and every process it started, after `SECS` seconds (it may be fractional). Exit 124.
Default: `CALLAI_TIMEOUT`, then `timeout` in the config file, then no limit. In a fan-out, a timeout is
that harness's failed result, and the others keep running.

## Behaviour

### `--permission LEVEL`

`default` (add nothing), `read-only`, `auto` or `bypass`, translated to each harness's flags. A level a
harness can't honour is refused (exit 2): opencode refuses `read-only` and `auto`, and hermes refuses
`read-only`. `bypass` prints a warning on stderr. What each level really allows:
[Permissions](../concepts/permissions.md). The exact flags: [Harnesses](harnesses.md).

### `--system-prompt SYSTEM_PROMPT`

Extra system instructions:

| Harness | Passed as |
|---|---|
| claude-code | `--system-prompt S` (replaces claude's own) |
| codex | `-c developer_instructions="S"` (a developer message) |
| pi | `--system-prompt S` (replaces pi's own) |
| hermes | the `HERMES_EPHEMERAL_SYSTEM_PROMPT` environment variable |
| grok | `--system-prompt-override S` (replaces grok's own) |
| opencode | refused (exit 2): `opencode run` has no such option |

### `--resume SESSION_ID`

Continue the session with this id (the `session_id` from `-o json` or a `result` event). Mapped per
harness: [table](harnesses.md#session-flags). An id that is empty or starts with `-` is refused.

### `--continue`

Continue the harness's most recent session. There's no `-c` short form, because `-c` is `--command`.
It can't be combined with `--resume`. hermes refuses it, because it only continues its interactive
sessions: use `--resume`.

## Inspecting

### `--dry-run`

Print the exact harness command line and exit 0, without running it or needing it installed. Text:
one shell-quoted line, preceded by `NAME=value` for any environment variables callai would set. With
`-o json` or `-o stream-json`: `{"argv": [...]}`, plus `"env": {...}` when there are any. In a fan-out:
one line per harness, or `{"runs": [...]}`. [Shapes](output.md#--dry-run).

### `-v`, `--verbose`

Copy the harness's stderr to callai's stderr as it arrives. It's still captured for the result.
Without `-v`, it's shown only when the run fails.

### `--list-harnesses`

List every supported harness: its binary (including one set in the config file), where it is on
`PATH`, and its `--version`, or where to install it. With `-o json`, one object. [Shape](output.md#--list-harnesses).

### `--version`, `-h` / `--help`

Print callai's version or help and exit 0.

## Passing arguments to the harness

### `--`

Everything after a bare `--` is passed to the harness unchanged, after callai's own flags and before
the prompt. callai's flags must come before it. Not allowed with several harnesses (exit 2); use
`[harnesses.<name>] extra_args` in the config file instead.

```bash
callai -n opencode -p "Explain main.py" --dry-run -- --agent build
```

```text
opencode run --format json --print-logs --log-level ERROR --agent build -- Explain main.py
```

## Environment variables

| Variable | Default for |
|---|---|
| `CALLAI_HARNESS_NAME` | `-n` |
| `CALLAI_MODEL` | `-m` |
| `CALLAI_TIMEOUT` | `--timeout` |
| `CALLAI_STDIN_WAIT` | seconds to wait for piped input with `-p` (default `3`, `0` = don't wait) |
| `CALLAI_CONFIG` | config file path (must exist) |

Details: [Configuration](configuration.md#environment-variables).

See also: [Exit codes and errors](errors.md) · [Output formats](output.md)

<!-- source: reference/python-api.md -->
# Python API reference

Everything `import callai` gives you. Standard library only; Python 3.11+.

```python
import callai

result = callai.run("codex", "Fix the failing test", permission="auto", timeout=600)
```

## `callai.run`

```python
callai.run(
    harness_name: str,
    prompt: str,
    *,
    model: str | None = None,
    cwd: str | None = None,
    timeout: float | None = None,
    permission: str = "default",
    system_prompt: str | None = None,
    extra_args: Sequence[str] = (),
    resume: str | None = None,
    continue_session: bool = False,
    binary: str | None = None,
    on_event: Callable[[dict[str, Any]], None] | None = None,
) -> Result
```

Run one prompt through one harness and return its normalised result. The call blocks until the
harness finishes.

| Parameter | Meaning | CLI equivalent |
|---|---|---|
| `harness_name` | `"claude-code"`, `"codex"`, `"opencode"`, `"pi"`, `"hermes"` or `"grok"` | `-n` |
| `prompt` | The prompt, sent verbatim | `-p` |
| `model` | Passed to the harness verbatim (no alias resolution) | `-m` |
| `cwd` | Working directory for the harness | `-C` |
| `timeout` | Seconds before the harness and its children are killed | `--timeout` |
| `permission` | `"default"`, `"read-only"`, `"auto"` or `"bypass"` | `--permission` |
| `system_prompt` | Extra system instructions, where supported | `--system-prompt` |
| `extra_args` | Passed to the harness unchanged | after `--` |
| `resume` | Session id to continue | `--resume` |
| `continue_session` | Continue the harness's most recent session | `--continue` |
| `binary` | Executable to run instead of the harness's usual one on `PATH` | `[harnesses.<name>] binary` |
| `on_event` | Called with each [stream event](output.md#-o-stream-json) as it happens, from a background thread | `-o stream-json` |

**Returns** a [`Result`](#callairesult). A harness that ran and failed (bad model, refused tool,
non-zero exit) is a result with `is_error=True`, not an exception.

**Raises** a subclass of [`CallaiError`](#exceptions) when the run couldn't start or finish.

`run()` reads **no** `CALLAI_*` environment variables and **no** config file. There are no
`bypass` warnings either: what you pass is what runs. With `on_event`, the harness runs in its
streaming mode (claude `stream-json`, grok `streaming-json`). The last event is
`{"type": "result", **result.to_dict()}`.

## `callai.Result`

A frozen dataclass: the same data as the [`-o json` object](output.md#-o-json).

| Attribute | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `harness_name` | `str` | Harness that ran |
| `text` | `str` | Final answer, or the error message when `is_error` |
| `exit_code` | `int` | The harness's exit code |
| `is_error` | `bool` | Whether the run failed |
| `model` | `str \| None` | Model the harness reports using, else the requested one |
| `duration_ms` | `int \| None` | Wall-clock run time |
| `session_id` | `str \| None` | For `resume=` |
| `usage` | `dict[str, int] \| None` | `{"input_tokens", "output_tokens"}`; input counts cache reads and writes |
| `cost_usd` | `float \| None` | Cost, when the harness reports it (claude, opencode, pi) |
| `argv` | `tuple[str, ...]` | The exact command that ran |
| `raw_stdout`, `raw_stderr` | `str` | The harness's own output, unparsed (not in `to_dict()`) |

| Method | Returns |
|---|---|
| `to_dict()` | The `-o json` object as a new `dict` (key order as documented) |
| `with_updates(**changes)` | A copy with some fields changed |

## Exceptions

| Class | Raised when | `exit_code` |
|---|---|---|
| `callai.CallaiError` | Base class of all below | 1 |
| `callai.UsageError` | Invalid argument; an option the harness can't honour; unknown harness | 2 |
| `callai.HarnessNotFound` | The binary isn't on `PATH` (or `binary=` doesn't exist) | 127 |
| `callai.HarnessTimeout` | `timeout` expired; the process group was killed | 124 |
| `callai.Interrupted` | Ctrl-C (SIGINT forwarded to the harness) | 130 |

`str(exc)` is the message the CLI prints after `callai: error:`. Every message is listed in
[Exit codes and errors](errors.md).

```python
import callai

try:
    result = callai.run("opencode", "Explain main.py", permission="read-only")
except callai.UsageError as exc:
    print("can't do that:", exc)
```

```text
can't do that: --permission read-only: opencode has no read-only mode (its plan agent still allows shell commands); pass `-- --agent plan` yourself if that is acceptable
```

## Other names

`callai.main(argv=None) -> int` runs the CLI in-process (what the `callai` command calls) and returns its
exit code. The adapter registry (`callai.adapters`) is internal; see
[Add a new harness](../guides/add-a-harness.md).

See also: [8. Use callai from Python](../tutorial/08-python-api.md) · [Output formats](output.md)

<!-- source: reference/output.md -->
# Output formats reference

Exactly what callai prints for each `-o` value, `--dry-run`, `--list-harnesses` and fan-out. JSON is
always UTF-8, one object per line.

## `-o text`

The default. The answer (`text`) followed by a newline, on stdout. On failure, stdout is empty and
stderr gets the harness's own stderr (unless `-v` already showed it) plus the error text, if it isn't
already in that stderr. Exit code as in [Exit codes](errors.md#exit-codes).

## `-o json`

One object, the same for every harness:

```json
{
  "harness_name": "codex",
  "model": null,
  "text": "pong",
  "exit_code": 0,
  "is_error": false,
  "duration_ms": 6979,
  "session_id": "01a19506-c5ee-7893-ab89-d0f6b04924a4",
  "usage": {"input_tokens": 11, "output_tokens": 2},
  "cost_usd": null,
  "argv": ["codex", "exec", "--json", "--skip-git-repo-check", "--", "Reply with exactly: pong"]
}
```

| Key | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `harness_name` | string | The `-n` name that ran |
| `model` | string \| null | Model the harness reports using; else the requested `-m` (after alias resolution); else `null` |
| `text` | string | Final answer, or the error message when `is_error` |
| `exit_code` | integer | The harness's exit code |
| `is_error` | boolean | From the harness's explicit error signal, or a non-zero exit |
| `duration_ms` | integer | Wall-clock time of the harness run |
| `session_id` | string \| null | Use with `--resume` |
| `usage` | object \| null | `input_tokens` (all prompt tokens, cache reads and writes included) and `output_tokens` |
| `cost_usd` | number \| null | When the harness reports cost (claude, opencode, pi; codex, hermes and grok don't) |
| `argv` | array of strings | The exact command that ran |

Keys are always present, in this order. Unknown values are `null`. With a failure, stdout still has
the object, and stderr has the harness's stderr.

## `-o stream-json`

One JSON object per line, flushed as each event happens:

```json
{"type": "start", "harness_name": "pi", "model": "stub/stub-model", "argv": ["pi", "--mode", "json", "--model", "stub/stub-model", "--", "Reply with exactly: pong"]}
{"type": "text", "text": "pong"}
{"type": "result", "harness_name": "pi", "model": "stub/stub-model", "text": "pong", "exit_code": 0, "is_error": false, "duration_ms": 1047, "session_id": "01a19507-07fe-7550-b76e-7a5f6b29a908", "usage": {"input_tokens": 11, "output_tokens": 2}, "cost_usd": 0, "argv": ["pi", "--mode", "json", "--model", "stub/stub-model", "--", "Reply with exactly: pong"]}
```

| `type` | Keys | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `start` | `harness_name`, `model`, `argv` | First, once the binary is found. Not written if it isn't (exit 127). |
| `text` | `text` | Assistant text: whole blocks (claude, codex, opencode) or pieces (pi, grok). |
| `tool_use` | `id`, `name`, `input` | `name` and `input` are the harness's own (`Bash`, `{"command": "ls"}`). |
| `tool_result` | `id`, `is_error`, `output` | `id` matches the `tool_use`. `is_error` for a failed or refused call. |
| `result` | every `-o json` key | Always last, failures included. Missing only on timeout (124) or Ctrl-C (130). |

hermes has no event stream: `start` and `result` only. In a [fan-out](#fan-out), every event also
carries `harness_name`.

## `-o raw`

The harness's own stdout and stderr, byte for byte, without parsing. The exit code is the harness's. Not
allowed with several harnesses.

## `--dry-run`

Text, one shell-quoted command per line, with environment variables first:

```text
HERMES_EPHEMERAL_SYSTEM_PROMPT='Be terse.' hermes chat -Q --source tool --query=hi
```

With `-o json` or `-o stream-json`:

```json
{"argv": ["hermes", "chat", "-Q", "--source", "tool", "--query=hi"], "env": {"HERMES_EPHEMERAL_SYSTEM_PROMPT": "Be terse."}}
```

`env` is present only when callai sets variables. With several harnesses: one text line each, or
`{"runs": [{"harness_name": "…", "argv": […], "env": {…}}, …]}`.

## `--list-harnesses`

Text, one line per harness:

```text
claude-code  claude     2.1.316 (Claude Code)  /opt/node22/bin/claude
```

A missing harness shows `not installed (see <install URL>)`. If the binary prints no version,
`version unknown` appears instead. With `-o json`:

```json
{"harnesses": [{"harness_name": "claude-code", "binary": "claude", "path": "/opt/node22/bin/claude", "version": "2.1.316 (Claude Code)", "install_url": "https://code.claude.com/docs/en/setup"}]}
```

(One entry per harness; `path` and `version` are `null` when it isn't installed.)

## Fan-out

With `-n a/b`, `-n a,b` or `-n all`, results come in the order given:

| Format | Shape |
|---|---|
| text | `== name ==` then the answer, per harness. A failure is `== name (failed, exit N) ==` then its error text. |
| json | `{"results": [<-o json object>, …]}` |
| stream-json | Every harness's events interleaved as they happen, each with `harness_name` |
| raw | Not allowed (exit 2) |

A failed harness's own stderr goes to stderr after a `--- name stderr ---` line. Harnesses skipped
by `-n all` are reported on stderr as `callai: skipping <name>: <reason>`.

See also: [Normalised output](../concepts/normalised-output.md) · [Exit codes and errors](errors.md)

<!-- source: reference/configuration.md -->
# Configuration reference

Every setting callai reads outside its flags: the config file and environment variables. The Python
API ignores both.

## Precedence

For each setting, the first source that sets it wins:

| Setting | 1. Flag | 2. Environment | 3. Config, per harness | 4. Config, top level | 5. Default |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| harness | `-n` | `CALLAI_HARNESS_NAME` | — | `default_harness` | none (error) |
| model | `-m` | `CALLAI_MODEL` | `[harnesses.<name>] model` | `model` | the harness's own |
| timeout | `--timeout` | `CALLAI_TIMEOUT` | — | `timeout` | no limit |
| harness binary | — | — | `[harnesses.<name>] binary` | — | from `PATH` |
| extra harness args | after `--` (added last) | — | `[harnesses.<name>] extra_args` (added first) | — | none |

Model [aliases](#aliases) are resolved after the model is chosen.

## The config file

Location, first that applies:

1. `$CALLAI_CONFIG`: must exist, or exit 2;
2. `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/callai/config.toml`;
3. `~/.config/callai/config.toml`.

The file is optional, and a missing default file is fine. It's TOML, read with Python's `tomllib`.
Unknown keys, unknown harness names and wrong types stop callai (exit 2) with a message naming the file.

```toml
default_harness = "claude-code"
model = "fast"
timeout = 600

[harnesses.codex]
binary = "~/bin/codex"
model = "gpt-5-codex"
extra_args = ["--skip-git-repo-check"]

[aliases]
fast  = { claude-code = "haiku", codex = "gpt-5-codex-mini", opencode = "anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5" }
smart = { claude-code = "opus",  codex = "gpt-5-codex" }
```

### `default_harness`

String: one of `claude-code`, `codex`, `opencode`, `pi`, `hermes`, `grok`. Used when there's no `-n` and
no `CALLAI_HARNESS_NAME`.

### `model`

String: the default model for every harness, usually an alias.

### `timeout`

Positive number of seconds.

### `[harnesses.<name>]`

One table per harness (the name must be a supported harness):

| Key | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `binary` | non-empty string | Executable to run instead of the usual binary from `PATH`; `~` is expanded. Also used by `--list-harnesses` and `-n all`. |
| `model` | string | This harness's default model; beats the top-level `model`. |
| `extra_args` | list of strings | Passed to the harness before any arguments after `--`. Also used in fan-out, where `--` isn't allowed. |

### `[aliases]`

Each key is an alias name; its value maps harness names to that harness's model:

```toml
[aliases]
fast = { claude-code = "haiku", codex = "gpt-5-codex-mini" }
```

When the chosen model (from any source) is an alias name, it's replaced by the entry for the harness
being run. A model that isn't an alias passes through unchanged. An alias without an entry for that
harness is an error (`model alias 'fast' has no entry for pi`), rather than sending `fast` as a model
name.

## Environment variables

| Variable | Value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `CALLAI_HARNESS_NAME` | a harness name, `a/b`, `a,b` or `all` | Default for `-n` |
| `CALLAI_MODEL` | model or alias | Default for `-m` |
| `CALLAI_TIMEOUT` | positive number | Default for `--timeout`; anything else is exit 2 |
| `CALLAI_STDIN_WAIT` | number ≥ 0 (default `3`) | With `-p`, how long to wait for input on an idle stdin pipe before warning and continuing |
| `CALLAI_CONFIG` | path | Config file to use; must exist |
| `CALLAI_LIVE`, `CALLAI_LIVE_TIMEOUT` | `all` or names; seconds | Test suite only: enable live smoke tests |

An empty value counts as unset. `CALLAI_TOOL`, the old name of `CALLAI_HARNESS_NAME`, is rejected
with a message telling you to rename it.

Variables the **harnesses** read (`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `XAI_API_KEY`, `HERMES_HOME`, …)
pass through to them unchanged. callai adds only what an option needs, for example
`HERMES_EPHEMERAL_SYSTEM_PROMPT` for hermes's `--system-prompt`.

See also: [7. Set your defaults](../tutorial/07-defaults.md) · [Command line](cli.md)

<!-- source: reference/harnesses.md -->
# Harnesses reference

Exactly how callai invokes each harness, and what each one supports. Every row was verified against the
real CLI at the version shown. `--dry-run` prints the full command for any combination.

## Summary

| `-n` | Binary | Base command | Model flag | Output mode used | Verified with |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `claude-code` | `claude` | `claude -p --output-format json -- PROMPT` | `--model M` | one JSON object | claude 2.1.314 (and live) |
| `codex` | `codex` | `codex exec --json --skip-git-repo-check -- PROMPT` | `--model M` | JSON lines | codex-cli 0.166.0 |
| `opencode` | `opencode` | `opencode run --format json --print-logs --log-level ERROR -- WORDS…` | `--model provider/model` | JSON lines | opencode 1.19.5 |
| `pi` | `pi` | `pi --mode json -- PROMPT` | `--model provider/id` | JSON lines | pi 1.4.0 |
| `hermes` | `hermes` | `hermes chat -Q --source tool --query=PROMPT` | `-m M` (provider from hermes's config) | plain text | hermes-agent 0.19.0 |
| `grok` | `grok` | `grok --output-format json --single=PROMPT` | `--model M` | one JSON object | grok 1.0.70 |

## Permission flags

| `--permission` | claude-code | codex | opencode | pi | hermes | grok |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `default` | — | — | — | — | — | — |
| `read-only` | `--permission-mode plan` | `--sandbox read-only` | refused | `--tools read,grep,find,ls --no-mcp` | refused | `--tools read_file,grep,list_dir --disallowed-tools search_tool,use_tool` |
| `auto` | `--permission-mode acceptEdits` | `--sandbox workspace-write` | refused | `--tools read,grep,find,ls,edit,write --no-mcp` | `-t file` | `--allow Write --allow Edit` |
| `bypass` | `--dangerously-skip-permissions` | `--dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox` | `--auto` | — (pi's default already allows everything) | `--yolo` | `--permission-mode bypassPermissions` |

What these really allow: [Permissions](../concepts/permissions.md#verified-behaviour).

## Session flags

| | claude-code | codex | opencode | pi | hermes | grok |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--resume ID` | `--resume ID` | `exec … resume ID -- PROMPT` | `--session ID` | `--session ID` | `--resume ID` | `--resume=ID` |
| `--continue` | `--continue` | `exec … resume --last -- PROMPT` | `--continue` | `--continue` | refused | `--continue` |

codex's `resume` subcommand rejects `--sandbox`. callai puts exec's own options (including `--sandbox`
and `extra_args`) before `resume`, so they still apply to the resumed run.

## Other options

| | claude-code | codex | opencode | pi | hermes | grok |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--system-prompt S` | `--system-prompt S` | `-c developer_instructions="S"` | refused | `--system-prompt S` | env `HERMES_EPHEMERAL_SYSTEM_PROMPT` | `--system-prompt-override S` |
| `-o stream-json` | `--output-format stream-json --verbose` | unchanged | unchanged | unchanged | unchanged (no events) | `--output-format streaming-json` |
| Refused prompts | — | — | — | starts with `@` | — | starts with `/` |
| Reports model used | yes | no | no | yes | no | yes |
| Reports tokens / cost | yes / yes | yes / no | yes / yes | yes / yes | no / no | yes / no |

## Per-harness notes

### claude-code

`claude -p` with JSON output. `is_error` comes from claude's `is_error`, not `subtype`: claude reports
`"subtype": "success"` alongside `"is_error": true` for an unknown model. Run as root, claude refuses
`bypass` unless you set `IS_SANDBOX=1`. Install: <https://code.claude.com/docs/en/setup>.

### codex

`codex exec --json`. The answer is the last `agent_message` item, and a failure is `turn.failed` or
a non-zero exit. `error` items such as "model metadata not found" are warnings, not failures.
`--skip-git-repo-check` lets codex run outside a git repository. Install: <https://developers.openai.com/codex/cli>.

### opencode

`opencode run --format json`. The prompt is passed as separate words, because opencode quotes any
argument containing a space. `--print-logs --log-level ERROR` puts the real failure reason on stderr,
which callai reports. In `opencode run`, `-p` means password and `-c` means continue: pass harness
flags after `--` with care. Install: <https://opencode.ai/docs/>.

### pi

`pi --mode json`. pi exits 0 even when the model call fails, so failure comes from the assistant
message's `stopReason`. A prompt starting with `@` would be read as a file to attach, so callai refuses
it. Install: <https://pi.dev/docs/latest/quickstart>.

### hermes

`hermes chat -Q --source tool`, not `hermes -z`, which approves every tool call. The answer is stdout
without hermes's display lines (those end in `\r\n`), and the session id comes from stderr.
`--source tool` keeps callai's runs out of your session list, which is also why hermes `--continue`
can't find them. It has no read-only toolset, and it reports no tokens or cost. Install:
<https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/>.

### grok

xAI's official Grok Build CLI (`@xai-official/grok`). The prompt goes in one final `--single=PROMPT`
element, because `-p` has no `--` escape. A prompt starting with `/` is run as a slash command, even
after spaces, so callai refuses it. A refused tool call exits 0 with `stopReason: cancelled`, which
callai reports as an error (exit 1). Install: <https://x.ai/cli>.

> [!WARNING]
> `@vibe-kit/grok-cli` (superagent-ai) also installs a `grok` command with different flags. callai
> doesn't support it.

See also: [Add a new harness](../guides/add-a-harness.md) · [Installation](../getting-started/installation.md)

<!-- source: reference/errors.md -->
# Exit codes and errors reference

Every exit code and every message callai prints, with its cause and fix. Errors appear on stderr as
`callai: error: <message>`. Usage errors (exit 2) are preceded by the usage line. In Python, the same
message is `str(exc)`.

## Exit codes

| Code | Meaning | Python |
|---|---|---|
| `0` | Success (every harness, in a fan-out) | — |
| `1` | The harness reported an error but exited 0 | `result.is_error`, `result.exit_code == 0` |
| `2` | [Usage error](#usage-errors): nothing ran | `UsageError` |
| `124` | [Timed out](#timed-out) | `HarnessTimeout` |
| `127` | [Harness not installed](#harness-not-installed) | `HarnessNotFound` |
| `130` | [Interrupted](#interrupted) | `Interrupted` |
| other | The harness's own failure code | `result.is_error`, `result.exit_code` |

In a fan-out, the exit code is 0 if every harness succeeded, otherwise the first failure's in the order
given.

## Usage errors

All exit 2, before any harness runs.

### No harness given

```text
no harness given: use -n/--name, set CALLAI_HARNESS_NAME, or set default_harness in the config file
```

**Fix:** pass `-n`, or set a default ([Configuration](configuration.md)).

### Unknown harness

```text
unknown harness '<name>'; choose from claude-code, codex, opencode, pi, hermes, grok
```

**Fix:** use one of the listed names. The names are callai's (`claude-code`), not the binary's
(`claude`).

### No prompt

```text
a prompt is required: use -p PROMPT or pipe it on stdin
```

**Cause:** no `-p`, and stdin was empty or a terminal. **Fix:** pass `-p`, or pipe the prompt in.

### Permission level not supported

```text
--permission read-only: opencode has no read-only mode (its plan agent still allows shell commands); pass `-- --agent plan` yourself if that is acceptable
--permission auto: opencode has no 'auto-approve edits only' mode (--auto approves everything); use --permission bypass or the default
--permission read-only: hermes has no read-only toolset (its `file` toolset can write); use the default or --permission auto
```

**Cause:** the harness has no way to honour the level, and callai won't give it more access than you
asked for. **Fix:** choose another level or another harness, or accept the alternative the message
names. [Permissions](../concepts/permissions.md#failing-closed).

### System prompt not supported

```text
opencode run has no system prompt option; drop --system-prompt
```

### Prompt would be run as a command

```text
grok runs a prompt starting with '/' as a slash command (e.g. /compact), even after leading spaces, and has no escape; start the prompt with other text
pi reads a prompt starting with '@' as a file to attach, and has no escape; start the prompt with other text (e.g. a space)
```

**Fix:** start the prompt with other text.

### `--resume` and `--continue`

```text
use --resume or --continue, not both
--resume: empty session id
--resume: a session id can't start with '-' (the harness would read it as an option)
--continue: hermes only continues its most recent interactive session, not callai's runs; use --resume with the session_id callai reported
```

### Fan-out

```text
-n <value>: use '/' (parallel) or ',' (one after another), not both
-n <value>: empty harness name
-n <value>: <name> is listed twice
-n <value>: 'all' can't be combined with other harnesses
-o raw needs a single harness (several raw outputs can't be told apart)
arguments after -- go to one harness; for several, set [harnesses.<name>] extra_args in the config file
-n all: every installed harness refused these options
<harness>: <reason>
```

The last form is a harness in an explicit list refusing an option. The whole call stops before
anything runs. With `-n all`, the harness is skipped instead, and stderr says
`callai: skipping <harness>: <reason>`.

### Working directory

```text
--cwd '<dir>' is not a directory
```

### Environment variables

```text
CALLAI_TIMEOUT must be a positive number of seconds, got '<value>'
CALLAI_STDIN_WAIT must be a number of seconds >= 0, got '<value>'
CALLAI_TOOL was renamed to CALLAI_HARNESS_NAME; set that instead
```

### Config file

Each of these is prefixed with the file's path (`<path>: …`):

```text
CALLAI_CONFIG points at <path>, which doesn't exist
<path>: invalid TOML (<details>)
<path>: cannot read config (<reason>)
<path>: unknown key '<key>'; allowed: aliases, default_harness, harnesses, model, timeout
<path>: [harnesses.<name>]: unknown key '<key>'; allowed: binary, extra_args, model
<path>: default_harness: unknown harness '<name>'; choose from …
<path>: [harnesses.<name>]: unknown harness; choose from …
<path>: [harnesses.<name>]: binary must be a non-empty string
<path>: [harnesses.<name>]: extra_args must be a list of strings
<path>: timeout must be a positive number of seconds, got <value>
<path>: model must be a string
<path>: [aliases] <alias> must map harness names to models, e.g. { codex = 'o3' }
<path>: [aliases] <alias>: unknown harness '<name>'; choose from …
```

**Fix:** correct the key or value the message names. Typos are errors on purpose, so a misspelled
setting never silently does nothing.

### Invalid arguments (Python API)

The CLI's parser catches these first, so in practice you see them only from `callai.run()`:

```text
invalid output format '<value>'; choose from text, json, stream-json, raw
invalid permission '<value>'; choose from default, read-only, auto, bypass
timeout must be a positive number of seconds, got <value>
prompt must be a string
extra_args must be a sequence of strings
resume must be a session id string
```

### Model alias without an entry

```text
model alias '<alias>' has no entry for <harness>
```

**Fix:** add the harness to the alias in `[aliases]`, or pass a model name with `-m`.

## Harness not installed

```text
harness binary '<binary>' not found on PATH (needed for --name <harness>); install it: <install URL>
-n all: none of the supported harnesses is installed (see callai --list-harnesses)
```

Exit 127. **Fix:** install the harness ([Installation](../getting-started/installation.md)), or point
`[harnesses.<name>] binary` at it.

## Timed out

```text
'<binary>' timed out after <secs>s and was killed
```

Exit 124. The harness and every process it started were killed. **Fix:** a larger `--timeout`, or a
smaller task. In a fan-out, this becomes that harness's failed result (`== name (failed, exit 124) ==`),
and the others carry on.

## Interrupted

```text
interrupted
```

Exit 130, after Ctrl-C. callai forwards SIGINT to the harness's process group, waits briefly, then
kills whatever is left. In a fan-out it stops every harness.

## Warnings

These go to stderr and don't change the exit code:

```text
callai: warning: no stdin data received in 3s, proceeding without it. Redirect stdin (< /dev/null) to skip the wait, or set CALLAI_STDIN_WAIT to wait longer.
callai: warning: --permission bypass: <harness> will run every tool call without asking, including shell commands and writes outside the working directory.
callai: skipping <harness>: <reason>
```

## When the harness fails

The run happened, but the harness reported an error (bad model, refused tool, API error):
- `is_error` is `true`, and `text` is the harness's reason;
- the exit code is the harness's own, or 1 if it exited 0;
- callai copies the harness's stderr to its own stderr.

Example:

```text
There's an issue with the selected model (not-a-real-model-xyz). It may not exist or you may not have access to it. Run --model to pick a different model.
```

See also: [Use callai in scripts and CI](../guides/scripts-and-ci.md) · [FAQ](../faq.md)

<!-- source: faq.md -->
# FAQ and troubleshooting

Short answers to common questions and problems.

## Questions

### Which harness should I use?

The one you already have access to. callai doesn't change what a harness can do; it gives them all the
same interface. To compare them on your own task, run them all:
[Compare harnesses side by side](guides/compare-harnesses.md).

### Does callai send my code or prompts anywhere?

No. callai talks only to the harness CLI on your machine. The harness talks to its model provider, as
it would without callai.

### Does callai handle API keys or sign-in?

No. Each harness uses its own configuration (`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `XAI_API_KEY`, a
signed-in session, …), which callai passes through unchanged.

### Does callai retry, rewrite prompts or add system instructions?

No. It adds only what your flags ask for, and `--dry-run` shows exactly what will run. It doesn't
retry, because a retry might repeat side effects the agent already had.

### Why is `model` null in my JSON?

You didn't pass `-m`, and the harness (codex, opencode, hermes) doesn't report which model it used.
claude, pi and grok report it.

### Why does `-n all --permission read-only` skip some harnesses?

opencode and hermes have no read-only mode. Rather than run them with more access than you asked
for, `-n all` skips them and says so on stderr. An explicit list (`-n codex/opencode`) stops with an
error instead.

### Can I run the same harness with two different models at once?

Not with one `-n`: it lists harnesses, not models. Start two `callai` processes, or use
`callai.run()` from two threads.

### Is there a TypeScript or Rust version?

Not yet. A TypeScript port is planned, and both will be checked against the same
[conformance suite](../../conformance/README.md).

## Problems

### callai waits 3 seconds before starting

Your stdin is a pipe with nothing on it, which happens when a script or agent runs callai. With `-p`,
callai waits up to 3 seconds for piped input, then warns and continues. Add `< /dev/null`, or set
`CALLAI_STDIN_WAIT=0`.

### callai seems to hang

- Without `-p` (or with `-p -`), the prompt *is* stdin, so callai waits until the pipe closes. Pass
  `-p` or close the pipe.
- The agent may simply be working. Use `-v` to see its stderr live, or `-o stream-json` to see its
  steps. Use `--timeout` to put a limit on it.

### callai hangs on Windows when run from a script

On Windows, the 3-second stdin wait doesn't work on pipes, so `callai -p TEXT` with an open, silent
stdin waits until the pipe closes. Give it an empty stdin that closes, e.g. in `cmd.exe`:
`callai -n codex -p "…" < NUL`. (This case isn't tested on Windows yet.)

### "harness binary … not found on PATH" (exit 127)

Install the harness ([Installation](getting-started/installation.md)). If it's installed somewhere
unusual, set `[harnesses.<name>] binary = "/path/to/it"`. `callai --list-harnesses` shows what callai
finds.

### "--permission read-only: … has no read-only mode" (exit 2)

That harness can't honour the level ([Permissions](concepts/permissions.md#failing-closed)). Choose
another harness, or the alternative the message suggests.

### The answer is empty and `is_error` is true

The harness ran but failed. `text` has its reason, and callai's stderr has the harness's own stderr.
Common causes: a model name the harness doesn't know, a missing API key, or a tool call refused
because you didn't grant the permission.

### claude says `--dangerously-skip-permissions cannot be used with root/sudo privileges`

You're running as root with `--permission bypass`. claude refuses that unless `IS_SANDBOX=1` is set in
the environment. callai deliberately doesn't set it for you.

### grok wrote a file outside my project

grok's `auto` and `bypass` aren't limited to the working directory. Add its sandbox:
`callai -n grok … --permission auto -- --sandbox workspace` (Linux needs bubblewrap). See
[Permissions](concepts/permissions.md#grok-and-the-working-directory).

### hermes `--continue` is refused

hermes only continues interactive sessions, not the ones callai starts. Use
`--resume <session_id>` from the previous run's JSON.

### A harness updated and callai broke

callai was verified against specific harness versions (see [Harnesses](reference/harnesses.md#summary)).
Run `callai --dry-run …` and the harness's own `--help` to see what changed. From the project folder,
`make install.<harness>` reinstalls the verified version. Please report what changed.

See also: [Exit codes and errors](reference/errors.md)
